00c8cda2-d033-5a89-89e5-4f6a4483e3da.dates: Late 19th century – begining of the 20th century
00c8cda2-d033-5a89-89e5-4f6a4483e3da.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph The Hijaz Railways
00c8cda2-d033-5a89-89e5-4f6a4483e3da.description2: The Hijaz Railway was a narrow-gauge railway (1,050mm/3ft, 5 11⁄32 in track gauge) that ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. It got no further than Medina, 400 kilometres (250mi) short of Mecca, due to the interruption of the construction works caused by the outbreak of World War I.

019530a6-cc5d-510e-8a02-0122394f5817.name: Revolver
019530a6-cc5d-510e-8a02-0122394f5817.description: The Lebel Revolver was the standard issue sidearm in the French military during the First World War, produced in Saint Etienne and used by the French army between 1892 and before 1924. The 1892 Model is a double/single action, six round cylinder revolver that fires 8-millimetre rounds. It was issued to officers in the French Army, Navy, and National Gendarmerie, amongst others. It is commonly called the Lebel Revolver after the gun designer Colonel Nicolas Lebel. For loading and releasing the empty cases, the chambers are accessed through swinging the cylinder to the right. Originally chambered for an 8mm gunpowder cartridge round, later models issued during World War I and thereafter fired the same 8mm cartridge loaded with smokeless powder. Serial number 21093.

03110c09-4d62-5959-a659-ea8534ac6e28.archival: “Bollettino della Società geografica”, serie IV, 1901, vol. II, n. 6, p. 548
03110c09-4d62-5959-a659-ea8534ac6e28.second_name: Egyptian and migrant labourers working on the construction of the first dam on the Nile
03110c09-4d62-5959-a659-ea8534ac6e28.description2: In 1900, Count Giulio d’Aspremont, an Italian diplomat, visited the construction site of the first dam across the Nile (today known as the Aswan Low Dam or Old Aswan Dam). He took several pictures of the works and of the monuments on the island of Philae that were going to be submerged by the water. He published some of them on the *Bulletin of the Italian Geographical Society*, where he wrote that up to 2,000 Italian workers were employed in the works (as stone-cutters, miners and masons), out of a total labour force of about 10,000 or 12,000; an Italian village had sprung up on the Nile banks, with modest little houses, trattorias and shops.

03762b34-622e-5cca-85b2-11ca849dd5d2.description2: The Hijaz Railway ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. The main purpose of the railway was to establish a connection between the capital of the Ottoman Empire and the seat of the Islamic Caliphate, and Hijaz in Arabia, the site of the holiest shrines of Islam and the holy city of Mecca, the destination of the Hajj annual pilgrimage. Another important reason was to improve the economic and political integration of the distant Arabian provinces into the Ottoman state, and to facilitate the transportation of military forces.

0377755d-a4a5-57ef-8cca-716b1fdb2ad1.name: Document recording the purchase of steamships
0377755d-a4a5-57ef-8cca-716b1fdb2ad1.description: A record from the archive of correspondence between the Sultan of Morocco Mulay al-Hasan I and his Minister of Foreign Affairs and representative in Tangier, Muhammad ibn al-‘Arabi al-Torres. It details Morocco’s order, from Italy, for the construction of a warship, the payment terms, constraints and currency exchange rates. In 1891, Morocco purchased four warships and a number of steamships.

088cf3bb-ffc3-56ca-8a23-9d69924c19fa.name: Port of Alexandria
088cf3bb-ffc3-56ca-8a23-9d69924c19fa.keywords: Alexandria Port; King Fouad I; Trips to Europe
088cf3bb-ffc3-56ca-8a23-9d69924c19fa.description2: The Port of Alexandria during the departure of King Fu`ad on a trip to Europe. The Eastern Port of Alexandria is one of the oldest ports in the world. It was established in 2000 BCE, at the ancient village of Rakotis, to serve the coastal areas of the Pharos island (now the area of Ra's al-Tin in Alexandria). To its west lies the Bay of Anfushi.

08b771ac-afdd-58cc-bc71-eaaef0f074bc.description: The first railway in Morocco was in the north of the country. Built in 1859, it connected Tétouan to the River Martil or Rio Martin as the Spanish – who built the railway – named it. Some solutions emerged at the end of the 19th century, but as this photograph from 1919 demonstrates, the equipment was still far too cumbersome to be used comfortably.

0b7f2149-f01d-5891-815e-947600259db6.name: *The drilling of an artesian well*
0b7f2149-f01d-5891-815e-947600259db6.artist: Artist: G. Dascher; engraver: L. Geisler
0b7f2149-f01d-5891-815e-947600259db6.description2: The purpose of the album *Les Colonies Françaises* was to highlight, amongst other things, the French "achievements" and technological innovations in the colonies, and thus legitimise their rule. This image shows the construction of an artesian well in Tunisia in the 19th century. In reality, however, this type of well was built by the French army in order to appease the populations in agricultural areas and thus better control them.

0c667bca-0934-5597-9606-a0052b8b5720.name: *Cairo, the Nile Dam*
0c667bca-0934-5597-9606-a0052b8b5720.second_name: Taken from Marcel Jusserand, *Souvenirs d'Egypte* (Memories of Egypt)
0c667bca-0934-5597-9606-a0052b8b5720.description2: The reign of Muhammad 'Ali Pasha was marked by a series of great changes, including attempts to take control of irrigation. The governor appointed French specialists, amongst whom was Linant de Bellefonds, and tasked them with the construction of a dam near Cairo. Linant de Bellefonds faced a great many difficulties during the construction, such as saving the pyramids, which the Pasha had wanted to destroy in order to supply the new dam with stone. The works were taken over by the engineer Eugène Mougel who added fortifications, as can be seen from this photograph, taken by a tourist at the beginning of the 20th century. The dam was completed c. 1835.

0df04b1e-0995-5f3a-a767-e848e62c8fbf.name: *The Bridge Carol I*
0df04b1e-0995-5f3a-a767-e848e62c8fbf.description2: The railroad bridge over the Danube that was built between 1890–1895 in South-Eastern Romania shortened the route of the Orient Express, a passenger train meant to connect Paris to Istanbul. The bridge made it possible for the Orient Express to reach Constanţa, a Black Sea port, from where ships went to Istanbul, whereas in the past the journey implied people being ferried on the Danube from Romania to Bulgaria, travelling by train to Varna (a Bulgarian Black Sea port) and then taking a ship to Istanbul. The “Carol I” bridge, which was designed by engineer Anghel Saligny and was at that time the longest in Europe, was inaugurated on 29 September 1895. In his inaugural speech, the king declared that “Romania is now owner of the shortest route between the northern seas and the countries of the Orient”.

0ee9442b-fe87-5668-a98a-944398b82de9.name: *Egypt. Suez canal.*
0ee9442b-fe87-5668-a98a-944398b82de9.keywords: Suez canal; Egypt; Ferdinand de Lesseps
0ee9442b-fe87-5668-a98a-944398b82de9.second_name: Taken from the collection *Lithiographies Représentant L'isthme de Suez*
0ee9442b-fe87-5668-a98a-944398b82de9.description2: The inauguration of the Suez Canal saw spectacular celebrations, attended by many European royalties. This was a huge victory for Ferdinand de Lesseps, who had sincerely hoped it would be a memorable and historical event. On his request, the painter Édouard Riou (1833–1900) produced a series of watercolours which were later published in *L’Album de l’Impératrice : Voyage Pittoresque à travers l’Isthme de Suez*.

11e4d236-bdc2-5339-827e-8d983887fbd6.description2: Private carriage of Queen Maria Pia, offered by her father, King Victor Emmanuel, when she married the Portuguese king D. Louis in 1862. The chariot is pulled by steam locomotive D. Luiz.

124efc2d-1a23-56df-83e7-543dbb950692.name: Port of Beirut
124efc2d-1a23-56df-83e7-543dbb950692.description: The Port of Beirut is the main port in Lebanon and it is one of the most beneficial commercial architecture in Lebanon that contributes the state’s revenue. It was founded in 1887 under the reign of the Ottomans and has since been the western-eastern link in the Middle East area. The Port of Beirut has a total area of 1,200,000 m2.
124efc2d-1a23-56df-83e7-543dbb950692.holder: Government of Lebanon; Gestation and exploitation of Port of Beirut (GEPB)
124efc2d-1a23-56df-83e7-543dbb950692.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Rita El Hachem, Julien El Khoury
124efc2d-1a23-56df-83e7-543dbb950692.history: Founded in 1887, the Port of Beirut is located on the eastern side of St Georges Bay, on Beirut's northern Mediterranean coast, west of the Beirut river. It is one of the largest and busiest ports of the Eastern Mediterranean. In early 90’s, a phase of development and reconstruction took place. The Port was rehabilitated and expanded to encompass 4 docks, 2 new quays (15 and 16) and new container terminal with 700,000 TEU/year capacities. The container terminal became operational in February 2005. It is equipped with 6 ship-to-shore gantry cranes (outreach 60m) and 18 rubbed tyred gantry cranes. The Port of Beirut has been selected as a transhipment hub for the 2nd and 3rd largest container shipping companies in the world.

1488ab73-2672-5641-a84a-174c9bfb4fd8.name: Perpetual calendar
1488ab73-2672-5641-a84a-174c9bfb4fd8.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
1488ab73-2672-5641-a84a-174c9bfb4fd8.dimensions: Height 130 mm, width 70 mm, depth 33 mm
1488ab73-2672-5641-a84a-174c9bfb4fd8.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
1488ab73-2672-5641-a84a-174c9bfb4fd8.materials: Nielloed silver, copper alloy, iron, wood, printed paper, printed textile
1488ab73-2672-5641-a84a-174c9bfb4fd8.description2: This perpetual calendar is contained within a cylindrical silver casing with a rounded shoulder. Four lateral knobs, two on either side, move the calendar's paper and textile elements, giving the month, the date and probably the day (this section is damaged). Above, a circular medallion contains the start year of the calendar, 1327 H/ 1909 AD.  The calendar is decorated all over with delicate niello deccoration. The front, with three superposed and elongated cartouche-shaped openings, is ornamented with a lobed panel containing naturalistic flower sprays. Below, a panel with three loop extensions contains an Arabic inscription - taqweem da'imi - that identifies the object's function. In the Tanzimat period, and up to 1926, the Mailya or Rumi calendar was introduced, which was based on the Julian solar calendar but started in the year of the Prophet's (pbuh) move from Makkah to Madina in 1 H/ 622 AD. It used old Syrian names for the months and was intended to ease the annual tax and fiscal calculations and payments.

154a0f2d-b51b-50e4-a764-5552e98c9b1a.name: A photo of the Irrigation Room at Fu`ad Agricultural Museum
154a0f2d-b51b-50e4-a764-5552e98c9b1a.dates: 16 January 1938 (Photo taken during the inauguration of the museum)
154a0f2d-b51b-50e4-a764-5552e98c9b1a.description2: The Fu`ad Agriculture Museum was considered the first of its kind in the Middle East and the Arab World during the 1930s. It was inaugurated during the time of King Faruq, the son of King Fu`ad, and houses a large number of collections related to agricultural and rural environments, as well as agricultural plants and animals.

1c45a682-1820-5eee-b604-862620e6fcea.description2: This oil on canvas painting shows a scene from daily life at the Tunis post and telegraph office, built on the Rue d'Italie (now Rue Charles-de-Gaulle). One of the busiest rooms, the revenue office's great hall is, with its tremendously high ceilings, an impressive example of neo-classical architecture. Featuring elements of carved plaster and a map of Tunisia on a central marble panel, this painting faithfully reproduces the opulence of this historic building.

1e164505-7b44-5ab0-8ab5-124407905064.name: Model of the brig *Mariţa*
1e164505-7b44-5ab0-8ab5-124407905064.description2: In 1834 Wallachia and Moldavia, which were under Ottoman suzerainty, were granted by the Ottoman Empire the right to sail on the Danube using their national banners. The first Romanian ship to sail under Romanian banner was the brig “Marița”, built in the naval dockyard of the Giurgiu port. Its owner was Wallachian politician Alexandru Vilara, who gave it the name of the wife of Alexandru II Ghica, Wallachia’s ruler between 1834-1842. “Marița” began its first trip in December 1834. Its destination was Istanbul, where it transported 300 kg of wheat. It returned in June 1835 after having been seriously damaged by two storms, one of which on its way back, when the crew had to throw overboard the wine purchased from Istanbul.

1f47ed93-cd30-5e50-a285-fa35fb1728c8.name: Mada'in Salih Railway Station
1f47ed93-cd30-5e50-a285-fa35fb1728c8.holder: Saudi Commission for Tourism and Antiquities
1f47ed93-cd30-5e50-a285-fa35fb1728c8.location: Northwest of Saudi Arabia in al-'Ula (Alula) region
1f47ed93-cd30-5e50-a285-fa35fb1728c8.history: Historically the Tribe of Lihyan was the first known Tribe settled in the area and founded the Kingdom of Lihyan in the "Oasis of Aula" in  the sixth century until the fourth BC. There is not much historical information about the Lihyanite but mentions that they allied themselves with the Nabataeans later. The largest settlement in the area was in the first century AD when the Nabateans made it as the second capital of  their kingdom after Petra in Jordan. The Nabateans dug their graves in the facades  of the mountains of the region , where there are about 132 tombs cut and carved in the rock. Nabataean state has fallen at the hands of the Romans in the second century AD.
1f47ed93-cd30-5e50-a285-fa35fb1728c8.keywords: Railway; station; Hijaz railway; Arabian Peninsula; history of the Hijaz railway; communication; innovation; route; pilgrimage; hajj; Ottoman; Germany; Abdul Hamid; abd al-hamid

1f47ed93-cd30-5e50-a285-fa35fb1728c8.description2: Mada'in Salih Station, which is located 25 kilometres north-east of al-'Ula City, was one of the main railway stations. The site contains seventeen building in addition to the ancient Islamic castle, and there is an old water pool and five wells folded with stones, as well as sixteen building of the railway station have been built in trimmed stones. The buildings had been converted into a museum tells the history of the Hijaz Railway.

1f9cc409-36e4-51f2-828e-77a94d820a08.name: Istanbul water pipeline map
1f9cc409-36e4-51f2-828e-77a94d820a08.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
1f9cc409-36e4-51f2-828e-77a94d820a08.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; History of Water in Ottoman Empire; Water; map
1f9cc409-36e4-51f2-828e-77a94d820a08.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The Cendere Hamidian Water Pump Station was built by Abdülhamid II in 1902. The station is located at an altitude of 34 metres above sea level. With its function, architectural design and mechanical equipment, the station is a unique reminder of Ottoman architecture. It pumped to Balmumcu and Beşiktaş – with water coming from 20 different pipes in Kağıthane, propelled by steam pump machines.

21301784-a7a9-5271-b156-37a91e6af337.name: Ma'an Railway Station
21301784-a7a9-5271-b156-37a91e6af337.author: Mohammad Najjar
21301784-a7a9-5271-b156-37a91e6af337.history: In 1900-1908, Sultan Abdul Hamid with the help and support of Germany established a Railway between Damascus and Mecca (1700 km) to facilitate transporting the pilgrims. The track from Medina to Mecca (400 km) was never realized. The cost of the project was estimated at approximately 5 million Ottoman golden liras, which were provided from: private donations, revenues of the Ottoman State from the sale of stamps, and a special tax upon all citizens for the railway. Construction of the narrow-gauge track (105cm) began in 1900 with a wire telegraph line along its side connecting Damascus with Medina across Amman with a total track length of 1303 km. Official inaugurations of the tracks and stations were scheduled to coincide with the accession of the Sultan to the throne in the month of September every year. The construction of the project ended in 1908.
21301784-a7a9-5271-b156-37a91e6af337.keywords: Hijaz; railway; station; pilgrimage; hajj; pilgrimage route; communication; telegraph; Jordan; Damascus; Mecca; Makka; Amman; Zarqa; Qatranah; Ma'an; Amman; Tabuk; Arabian Peninsula; Ottoman; Abd al Hamid; Germany; Meinsner
21301784-a7a9-5271-b156-37a91e6af337.description2: Ma'an station was one of the most important stations along the Hijaz railway. It consists of several buildings parallel to the railway that include a passengers' hall, maintenance workshops, water towers and the residence of the German engineer Meinsner who was in charge for the construction of the Hijaz railway. With its various components including the rails, steam engines, bridges and stations, the project stands as an industrial, architectural and engineering statement that had a huge influence on Jordan. The Amman-Ma'an Section was completed in September 1904. The Ma'an-Tabuk Section was completed in September 1906.

22ba355b-61ed-56c7-97f9-3b2325767140.name: *The Railway Station at Jaffa*
22ba355b-61ed-56c7-97f9-3b2325767140.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)

22ba355b-61ed-56c7-97f9-3b2325767140.description2: *The Railway Station at Jaffa* is a drawing included in the book *Palestine Past and Present* by Laura Jewry Valentine. In the chapters about Jaffa and Jerusalem, the description of the geography, religious history and climate focuses on the route of the Jaffa–Jerusalem railway. It provides an interesting report on this communication route, built by the French and opened on September 1892, connecting Jaffa to Jerusalem and various villages in between.

27b52e92-40ef-53b5-9de2-ba320998fdf0.name: Lisbon Astronomical Observatory
27b52e92-40ef-53b5-9de2-ba320998fdf0.holder: National Museum of Natural History and Science (MUHNAC) / Museums of the University of Lisbon

27b52e92-40ef-53b5-9de2-ba320998fdf0.history: The Observatory was constructed with the support and sponsorship of King Pedro V (1837–1861). It began operating in 1867 and its first director was Frederico Oom, followed by Campos Rodrigues (1836–1919), an internationally recognised astronomer and a creator of several scientific instruments. In 1995, the Observatory integrated the University of Lisbon.

27b52e92-40ef-53b5-9de2-ba320998fdf0.description2: The Lisbon Astronomical Observatory is the Portuguese national observatory. It has the legal responsibility of national timekeeping. It is located in the Tapada da Ajuda, a green area in the west of Lisbon. It is part of the Museums of the University of Lisbon/National Museum of Natural History and Science. It includes several buildings. It promotes activities regarding the public understanding of astronomy and astrophysics for diverse audiences. The Observatory has important collections: scientific instruments, mostly from the 19th and early 20th century; a Library, which is reference in Portugal, and an important historical archive.

28f9592c-7e7c-553c-be06-baac37d4447b.name: *The arrival of Suleiman Pasha, envoy of the Porte, in Giurgiu*
28f9592c-7e7c-553c-be06-baac37d4447b.second_name: *The arrival of the Ottoman army in Valahia*
28f9592c-7e7c-553c-be06-baac37d4447b.description2: In June 1848 revolution broke out in Wallachia, aiming to liberate the country from the Ottoman sovereignty. Prince Bibescu was deposed and a provisional government was installed. As a result, the sultan sent an army to Wallachia. The Ottoman army entered on the Romanian territory in July and the Porte’s representative, Suleiman Pasha, began negotiations with the Romanian revolutionary government. This chromolithograph is part of a series of German chromolithographs depicting episodes from the Revolution that took place in Wallachia in 1848. It shows the entrance of Süleyman Pasha, the Porte's envoy, accompanied by a part of his army of 20.000 soldiers, in Giurgiu, a port on the Danube, after having crossed the river. He is received by a Romanian delegation.

298f1be0-1a70-55ec-8567-86eda6c195f5.name: Revolver
298f1be0-1a70-55ec-8567-86eda6c195f5.description: This solid-frame, short-barrel pocket revolver was manufactured in Britain. This type of revolver became very popular and had been copied by many gun makers in different countries such as Belgium, Spain, and France among others. The American President James Garfield in 1881 was assassinated by one of these revolvers, probably an American copy of the British Bull Dog. This revolver is fitted with wooden grip plates. The cylinder is smooth and no serial number can be seen on it. The only engravement is what can be read as British Bull Dog at the top of the barrel. The base of the barrel was broken and mended.

2afaee38-c8b6-5f96-881c-e8b6d088c400.name: Amman Railway Station
2afaee38-c8b6-5f96-881c-e8b6d088c400.author: Mohammad Najjar
2afaee38-c8b6-5f96-881c-e8b6d088c400.history: In 1900-1908, Sultan Abdul Hamid with the help and support of Germany established a Railway between Damascus and Mecca (1700 km) to facilitate transporting the pilgrims. The track from Medina to Mecca (400 km) was never realized. The cost of the project was estimated at approximately 5 million Ottoman golden liras, which were provided from: private donations, revenues of the Ottoman State from the sale of stamps, and a special tax upon all citizens for the railway. Construction of the narrow-gauge track (105cm) began in 1900 with a wire telegraph line along its side connecting Damascus with Medina across Amman with a total track length of 1303 km. Official inaugurations of the tracks and stations were scheduled to coincide with the accession of the Sultan to the throne in the month of September every year. The construction of the project ended in 1908.
2afaee38-c8b6-5f96-881c-e8b6d088c400.keywords: Hijaz; railway; station; pilgrimage; hajj; pilgrimage route; communication; telegraph; Jordan; Damascus; Mecca; Makka; Amman; Zarqa; Qatranah; Ma'an; Amman; Tabuk; Arabian Peninsula; Ottoman; Abd al Hamid; Germany; Meinsner
2afaee38-c8b6-5f96-881c-e8b6d088c400.description2: Amman station was one of the main stations on the Hijaz railway. The location of the town of Amman along the Hijaz railroad had become a decisive factor in choosing Amman as the capital city of the Emirate of Transjordan in 1921. The station consists of several buildings including a passengers' waiting hall, maintenance depots and distinctive water towers. The various components of the project including the rails, steam engines, bridges and stations were an industrial, architectural and engineering statement that had a huge influence on Jordan. The Zarqa-Amman Section was completed in September 1903.

2bc79611-c941-5b21-81f7-7525e5e187ea.name: An example of Italian colonial propaganda describing 'The first railway engine crossing Libya, causing astonishment and panic among the Arabs'
2bc79611-c941-5b21-81f7-7525e5e187ea.author: Giulia Barrera
2bc79611-c941-5b21-81f7-7525e5e187ea.third_name: *'La prima locomotiva attraversa il suolo libico tra lo spavento e lo stupore degli arabi'*
2bc79611-c941-5b21-81f7-7525e5e187ea.second_name: A colonial postcard about the inauguration of the first railway in Libya
2bc79611-c941-5b21-81f7-7525e5e187ea.description2:
The railway in a colonial context was much more than a means of transport: it was a powerful symbol of modernity, of technological superiority of the colonisers over the colonised, and of mastery over the territory. The construction of railways in colonial situations was thus often celebrated by the colonialists’ popular press or in postcards, as in this case.  
In Libya, the Italians started building railroads from the first months of colonial rule. The first lines, inaugurated in 1912, connected Tripoli with Ain Zara (11 kms) and to Zanzur (39 kms). By the end of 1915, the railway lines in Libya amounted to 180 kilometres.

2beb8ede-81f6-5a62-aa22-de18127faa93.name: Photograph of Casablanca Railway Station
2beb8ede-81f6-5a62-aa22-de18127faa93.description: In 1908, the French General Albert d’Amade led the pacification of the Kabyle Berber peoples on the plains of Chaouia and also oversaw the construction of a railway line between Casablanca and Berrechid. By 1914, the railway was mainly used for the civil transportation of people and goods. This shot of Casablanca Station in 1920 depicts a train arriving at the station, where the passengers waiting to board appear to be European settlers and Moroccan notables.

2de7ed41-7aaa-5c57-b454-3ebdfa97e428.description: The front page of the newspaper *Le Petit Journal*, which depicts the installation of the wireless telegraph between Morocco and France in 1907.

2fd7dbb0-f684-52f4-93f3-b485ecf82f5e.name: Postcard: *The Strait of Gibraltar in the Future*
2fd7dbb0-f684-52f4-93f3-b485ecf82f5e.description: This curious postcard with a utopian vision of how the Strait of Gibraltar could become in the future was sent to the Marquis of Cerralbo by a friend, Gabriel Vich, but never received a stamp. Although it shows the address of the marquis, maybe it was posted inside an envelope or delivered, finally, on hand. This kind of ephemera was published by the fortnightly publication España en África (Spain in Africa), active in the first decades of the 20th century. The image represented is a beautiful commercial and geopolitical project that would have linked two continents with a 15 km bridge.

3018b07a-449e-5452-bb78-bbcfe4a57bdc.name: Beirut Port Train Station
3018b07a-449e-5452-bb78-bbcfe4a57bdc.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Rita El Hachem
3018b07a-449e-5452-bb78-bbcfe4a57bdc.description2: This station was used to deliver supplies from Beirut port to the main train station in Beirut, located in Mar Mikhael. The station was an important addition to the region's trade system, linking the sea routes the land routes.

341be9d6-6bac-5978-aa0e-844e03633f92.name: The port of Brăila
341be9d6-6bac-5978-aa0e-844e03633f92.archival: *Donau-Album. Malerische Reise von Regensburg bis Sulina. Album du Danube. Voyage pittoresque de Ratisbonne a Souline. Danube Album. A picturesque travel from Ratisbon to Suline. A Duna. Festöi utazas Regensburg-tol a Sulina torkolatig*, Vienna, A. Hartleben, 1880
341be9d6-6bac-5978-aa0e-844e03633f92.description2: In 1829, an annex to the peace treaty of Edirne, that was concluded after the Russo-Ottoman war of 1828-1829, concerned the Principalities of Wallachia and Moldavia. One of its provisions was that the Sublime Porte had to give back to Wallachia the three cities situated on the left bank of the Danube, which it had conquered in the 15h-16th centuries. Among these was Brăila, a port on the Danube annexed by the Ottomans at around 1540. After 1829 measures were taken by the local authorities for the modernization of Brăila. The port subsequently developed thanks to the growth of Wallachian commerce as a consequence of the fact that by the treaty of Edirne the Ottoman Empire granted the freedom of commerce to the Romanian Principalities. In 1838 Brăila was given the status of free port (with no or few customs duties).

3540af77-ea01-5e4b-bd04-3e31d3b139e4.name: Poster for the International Exhibition of Milan, 1906, depicting the opening of the Simplon Tunnel
3540af77-ea01-5e4b-bd04-3e31d3b139e4.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
3540af77-ea01-5e4b-bd04-3e31d3b139e4.author: Marina Minozzi
3540af77-ea01-5e4b-bd04-3e31d3b139e4.keywords: Printing; celebration of science; Positivism; industrialisation; industry; communication; road; railway; tunnel; working class; rights of workers; social topics; post-unitarian Italian society; health; work; labour; poverty; life expectancy
3540af77-ea01-5e4b-bd04-3e31d3b139e4.third_name: Manifesto dell'Esposizione Internazionale di Milano del 1906
3540af77-ea01-5e4b-bd04-3e31d3b139e4.description2: Leopoldo Metlicovitz worked as a lithographer and an illustrator. Among his works are illustrations for the Milanese newspaper *La Sera*, opera librettos and some cover pages of *Corriere della Sera*. He also made posters for an auto exhibition, an insurance company and the opening of the Simplon Tunnel in 1906. The erotic male nude recalls Michelangelo’s figures. The poster was chosen by the Committee of the International Exhibition despite the fact the it was not submitted within the competition. The artist depicts the personification of Progress and Science ideally leading the convoy towards the light beyond the tunnel. The tunnel, almost 20 kilometres long, was started following an 1895 agreement between Italy and Switzerland. The works were finished after long difficulties and the railway was opened on June 1, 1906 and celebrated at the Universal Exposition in Milan.

372e3810-b18e-5d0c-b107-9bd837cefb1e.name: Hijaz Railway Medal
372e3810-b18e-5d0c-b107-9bd837cefb1e.description: Medal of the Hijaz Railway fund. In September 1900, (the 25th anniversary of Sultan Abdul Hamid’s accession to throne) he addressed a call for all the Muslims all over the world to collect donations for establishing a railway between Damascus and the holy places to facilitate transporting the pilgrims. The call was responded to enthusiastically and with great support from all Muslims. Sultan Abdul Hamid II began the donations with 300,000 Ottoman gold lira, then kings and heads of Islamic world donated money or materials for setting the railway. The donations continued till 1907. On this occasion the sultan issued gold, silver and nickel medals to donors – for instance a nickel medal given to whoever donated 5-50 Lira, a silver medal for whoever donated 50-100 Lira and named them bey, and for donations of more than 100 Lira a gold medal and the title of Pasha. After that the donation become compulsory in which the officials disclaim a one month salary. This is a gilt nickel medal issued AH 1318 / AD 1900. On its obverse, within a wreath: tuğra of sultan Abdul Hamid II with "al-Ghazi" and form of locomotive and the date ١٣١۸ (AH 1318) below. On reverse, حميديه حجاز تيمور يولنه خدمت ايدن حميتمندانه مخصوص مدالية در ("Medal reserved to patriots who have served the Hamidiye Hijaz Railway") written in Divan script.

387152c3-f2e6-5090-9494-72805f950568.name: AUB Tramway
387152c3-f2e6-5090-9494-72805f950568.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Rita El Hachem
387152c3-f2e6-5090-9494-72805f950568.description2: The Beirut tramway, which covered a total of 12 kilometres in the city's centre, was opened in April 1908, during the Ottoman era. It was used all through the French Mandate era and was finally closed in September 1965.

3879757a-f06b-5c78-885b-5bf3ddf848b8.name: *Convoy of pilgrims*
3879757a-f06b-5c78-885b-5bf3ddf848b8.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
3879757a-f06b-5c78-885b-5bf3ddf848b8.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph pilgrims; pilgrimage; travelling
3879757a-f06b-5c78-885b-5bf3ddf848b8.description2: The Hijaz Railway was a narrow-gauge railway (1,050mm/​3ft, 5 11⁄32 in track gauge) that ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. It got no further than Medina, 400 kilometres (250mi) short of Mecca, due to the construction interruption caused by the outbreak of World War I. The main purpose of the railway was to establish a connection between Constantinople, the capital of the Ottoman Empire and the seat of the Islamic Caliphate, and Hijaz in Arabia, the site of the holiest shrines of Islam and the holy city of Mecca, the destination of the Hajj (annual pilgrimage).

388c8605-7211-5829-b5d8-9e4bc739a3af.name: Photograph of the extension of the telephone network in Tangier
388c8605-7211-5829-b5d8-9e4bc739a3af.description: A photograph taken in 1920 showing the installation of a new telegraph pole and wiring in order to extend the telephone network that had been installed in Tangier since 1883.
388c8605-7211-5829-b5d8-9e4bc739a3af.keywords: Telephone; technical innovations; communication; telephone network; photograph; visual document; changes in urban space; modernisation; modern city; city

39965ec4-de1b-54df-b13b-6f3de0ef242b.name: Morse transmitter
39965ec4-de1b-54df-b13b-6f3de0ef242b.keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication
39965ec4-de1b-54df-b13b-6f3de0ef242b.description2: In 1840, the Ministry of Post made an announcement describing the postal service, declaring it necessary in order to facilitate communication among people. The first regulations about the postal organisation were taken from French Law in 1840. Ottoman Postal Code included 44 specific headlines. In 1855 the first telegraph service and in 1909 the first telephone service were put into common use as a demonstration of modern communication. In order to improve the technology of the telegraph systems, Ottoman authorities imported well-known machines with trademarks such as Siemens & Halske and Western Electric. As a result of this technological improvement, Ottoman officials decided to establish a telegraph factory. Between 1869 and 1915, this factory produced many devices and accessories.

3a479e74-ad19-5334-a508-9d331c6ee9bd.name: 'Air force'
3a479e74-ad19-5334-a508-9d331c6ee9bd.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History

3a479e74-ad19-5334-a508-9d331c6ee9bd.second_name: An Italian cartoon protesting the Italian aerial bombing of Libyan villages
3a479e74-ad19-5334-a508-9d331c6ee9bd.description2: In 1911, in Libya, the newly founded Italian Air Force carried out the very first aerial bombing of civilian targets in world history. Italian anti-colonialists vocally protested such practice, as Scalarini’s cartoon shows.

3b3c9b35-91d8-5460-af41-e16d0268e789.name: Orient Express Poster
3b3c9b35-91d8-5460-af41-e16d0268e789.description2: The Orient Express, owned by the Wagon-Lits Company, connected Paris and Istanbul between 1883 and 1977. French, German, Austrian and Ottoman diplomats and civil servants were on board for its first journey. In the early years, the travellers stayed in different hotels in Istanbul but starting from 1895, passengers stayed exclusively in Pera Palace, which was bought by the Wagon-Lits Company. The Orient Express did not run during World War I, from 1914 to 1918.

3d995cca-af40-5f9f-8f23-5a077ea46883.name: Royal Decree to establish the post of *Makhzen*
3d995cca-af40-5f9f-8f23-5a077ea46883.description: The Royal Decree (dated 22 November 1892) of Mulay al-Hasan I asserted his *Makhzen* (royal authority) in order to take official control of the national post and transport services. In most localities, employees of this office were *‘Umana*, government officials, assisted by distributors.

3f3b04ad-02fe-52ca-a1d1-f83f2e45161f.name: Electrical command and control panel for Tejo Power Station I generators
3f3b04ad-02fe-52ca-a1d1-f83f2e45161f.author: Fátima Mendes
3f3b04ad-02fe-52ca-a1d1-f83f2e45161f.keywords: Electricity; Tejo power station, workers, innovation
3f3b04ad-02fe-52ca-a1d1-f83f2e45161f.description2: Using this control panel, the generators at Tejo Power Station I were controlled from the electrical point of view.  The mechanical circuits were controlled locally, which demonstrates well the difficulty in maintaining a uniform electricity supply for consumers at that time. Power fluctuations were fairly common, and these were mainly noticeable in the indoor lighting.

3f842425-2ace-59ff-ad9e-176b0b58c8f7.name: *Société les Affréteurs Réunis* \[…\] *Weekly, individual direct services from Rouen and Bordeaux-Bayonne to Algeria and Tunisia, and vice versa.*
3f842425-2ace-59ff-ad9e-176b0b58c8f7.description2: In Algeria and Tunisia, the French colonisers developed viticulture, cereal farming, and the extraction of minerals for export to France. The transportation of these goods took place by boat. Various firms emerged specifically for the transportation of this type of product, providing specialised ships and regular shipments between North Africa and the major French Atlantic ports. This map indicates the ports in Tunisia and Algeria and the railway networks connecting them (Oranais network, etc.).

4318dbfb-9a52-562e-8cea-6daf8a6a9d78.name: Rumelia Railway
4318dbfb-9a52-562e-8cea-6daf8a6a9d78.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
4318dbfb-9a52-562e-8cea-6daf8a6a9d78.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Anatolian Railways
4318dbfb-9a52-562e-8cea-6daf8a6a9d78.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

4489055a-7c22-5ee2-b83a-00d5a4759ff6.name: Tripoli railway station
4489055a-7c22-5ee2-b83a-00d5a4759ff6.description: This station first opened in 1911, connecting Tripoli to the Syrian city of Homs with a single track. It later became the terminus of the famous Orient Express line, operating in the 1920s, 1930s and 1940s. The station was nationalized in 1920 during the French Mandate following its destruction by the Ottoman forces during World War I.

4489055a-7c22-5ee2-b83a-00d5a4759ff6.keywords: Railway; Transport; Connection; Communication; Innovation; Station; Tripoli; Lebanon

4543ccbf-dceb-5300-941b-8c2f10ba3b29.name: The port of Galaţi
4543ccbf-dceb-5300-941b-8c2f10ba3b29.description2: After the Russian annexation of Bessarabia (the eastern part of Moldavia) in 1812 and until the restoration by Russia of Southern Bessarabia (1856), Galați remained Moldavia’s only port on the Danube. Understanding the city’s importance for Moldavia’s economy and wanting to ensure its development, prince Mihail Sturdza, who was appointed ruler of Moldavia by the Sublime Porte in 1834, issued in 1836 an act stipulating that Galați was to be a free port (with no or few customs duties) starting with March 1837. Also, a new neighborhood was to be built based on modern urban planning prescriptions and Galați received the right to organize annually five national fairs, during which traders from everywhere could sell any type of products.

45f8402d-e18b-5199-b2ae-ecde35d016ae.name: The train for VIP guests used during the inauguration of Luxor–Aswan Railway Line
45f8402d-e18b-5199-b2ae-ecde35d016ae.keywords: Egyptian Railways; Aswan Railway Line; Transportation in Egypt
45f8402d-e18b-5199-b2ae-ecde35d016ae.description2:
The inauguration of the Aswan Train Station, with \`Adli Yakan Pasha; Muhammad Najib al-Gharabli Pasha; Husayn Rushdi Pasha; Tharwat Pasha; Fathallah Barakat Pasha; Morkos Hanna Pasha; al-Dagwi Bek, director of Aswan; and Mahmud Shakir Bek, deputy undersecretary of the Ministry of Transportation in attendance. This project took about 10 months, its length is about 218 kilometres and its cost was about 267,000 pounds.  
The Luxor–Aswan line was very important as Aswan city was the centre of trade routes from Nubia and Sudan.

47fcbd3c-bf49-59d2-b9ac-7634939dbb18.name: Islamic pottery from Ephesus
47fcbd3c-bf49-59d2-b9ac-7634939dbb18.description2: Excavated by John Turtle Wood, an architect and surveyor. He was employed by the Ottoman Railway Company from 1858. Between 1863–1874 he excavated on behalf of the British Museum at ancient Ephesus, where he discovered the Temple of Artemis.

4859f5a8-7af7-59f7-8271-982ef083627b.name: *Fellahs* (peasants) use a *shadouf* to draw water from the Nile from a well.
4859f5a8-7af7-59f7-8271-982ef083627b.description2: Ernest Benecke (1817–1894), a French photographer of Anglo-German origins, was one of the first to be interested in the people rather than the monuments he saw during his travels in the Middle East. His pictures foreground daily life, as we can see from this photograph, which was taken in Egypt and shows a traditional mode of irrigation using the *shadouf*, a weighted appliance which allowed water to be poured from a well over a field.

49fa2453-a0f1-50d3-9c2e-b116b3fe9fdd.name: Frith photograph
49fa2453-a0f1-50d3-9c2e-b116b3fe9fdd.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
49fa2453-a0f1-50d3-9c2e-b116b3fe9fdd.description2: Francis Frith was one of the most successful commercial photographers from the 1850s and 1860s. He also established what was to become the largest photographic printing business in England. This image is part of the V&A's Francis Frith 'Universal Series' archive which consists of over 4000 whole-plate albumen prints predominantly of historical and topographical sites. Images such as these were highly desirable throughout the 1850s and 1860s. Frith's growing business coincided with many technological developments taking place within the field of photography. These developments changed and expanded the audience for photography and Frith's operation was well-prepared to provide for it and, it can be argued, worked to develop it employing a diverse range of publishing channels.

4acd8717-82fe-538c-b4c9-53b16ce962bb.name: The plan of Haydarpaşa Train Station
4acd8717-82fe-538c-b4c9-53b16ce962bb.description2: The original plan of Haydarpaşa Train Station, viewed from northern frontage. In 1871 Sultan Abdülaziz ordered a rail line to be built from Haydarpaşa to İzmit. Haydarpaşa station opened in 1872, and in 1888 the Anatolian Railway (CFOA) took over the line and the station. Since the station was built next to the Bosporus, freight trains would unload at Haydarpaşa and the freight would be transferred to ships. Haydarpaşa was chosen to be the northern terminus of the Baghdad Railway and the Hijaz Railway in 1904 and with rail traffic increasing, a new and larger building was required. The Anatolian Railway hired two German architects, Otto Ritter and Helmut Conu, to build the new building. They chose a neo-classical structure and construction started in 1906.

4b55c559-2654-5a6f-a502-72a32dfa2c6a.name: Photo of the Aswan Railways inauguration
4b55c559-2654-5a6f-a502-72a32dfa2c6a.keywords: Egyptian Railways; Aswan Railway Line; Transportation in Egypt
4b55c559-2654-5a6f-a502-72a32dfa2c6a.description2: The inauguration of the Aswan Train Station, with `Adli Yakan Pasha; Muhammad Najib al-Gharabli Pasha; Husayn Rushdi Pasha; Tharwat Pasha; Fathallah Barakat Pasha; Morkos Hanna Pasha; al-Dagwi Bek, director of Aswan; and Mahmud Shakir Bek, deputy undersecretary of the Ministry of Transportation in attendance. The Egyptian railway line was the first to be established in Africa and the Middle East, and the second worldwide after the United Kingdom. The establishment of the first railway line in Egypt began on 12 June 1851, and it became operable in 1854. The Egyptian railway construction project supervisor at that time was British engineer Robert Stephenson, son of the famous inventor of locomotives, George Stephenson. The Aswan train station is one of the most important railway lines constructed during the reign of King Fu`ad.

4bef9a7e-ee5d-50e6-bbc2-ad9258836fd3.name: Carlo de Rossetti (consul of the Grand Duke of Tuscany) gives notice of a new ferry boat service between Alexandria (Egypt) and Constantinople operated by a Tuscan steamship
4bef9a7e-ee5d-50e6-bbc2-ad9258836fd3.author: Cristina Francioli
4bef9a7e-ee5d-50e6-bbc2-ad9258836fd3.archival: AS Li, Governo civile e militare, b. 890
4bef9a7e-ee5d-50e6-bbc2-ad9258836fd3.third_name: *Notificazione concernente l’attivazione di corse regolari fra Alessandria e Costantinopoli, e viceversa, mediante il Battello a Vapore Toscano* Il Generoso, *ed il suo servizio*
4bef9a7e-ee5d-50e6-bbc2-ad9258836fd3.description2: The steamboat Il Generoso had three classes of service: the first-class ticket cost 42.5 Thalers and the second class one 30 Thalers; they both included meals. By contrast, the third-class ticket (12 Thalers) did not entitle one to meals. The trip lasted five days. According to the poster, the steamboat Il Generoso was equipped with “very confortable cabins and living rooms, including a special living room for ladies”.

4c12bb09-5654-50d7-9357-afc588c0f91d.name: Photograph of the dam of Sennar (Upper-Egypt) during its construction in April 1925
4c12bb09-5654-50d7-9357-afc588c0f91d.description2: Since antiquity, those living around the Nile had attempted to take advantage of the floods to better irrigate their lands. Many dams were built in the 20th century, most notably at Aswan (1902). The first Sudanese dam was built in 1925, in Sennar in the Blue Nile state, in order to irrigate the agricultural region of Gezira.

4ceec2b5-7808-56c2-b795-ced282fa861d.name: *24 hour optical telegraphy presented to the minister by a marine officer and used by the coast signalling services* (1802)
4ceec2b5-7808-56c2-b795-ced282fa861d.description2: The telegraph was an important piece of technology for Napoléon I, as it allowed him to send information quickly from both land and sea during the War of the First Coalition. A huge network of telegraph lines was created during his reign.

4e0e7286-5def-51f5-b4c3-162106c6828c.name: Silverware used on the Orient Express
4e0e7286-5def-51f5-b4c3-162106c6828c.description2: After the Crimean War, Ottoman authorities concluded that a railway connecting Europe with Istanbul was necessary. The construction of a new terminal building began on 11 February 1888. The terminal building is one of the most famous examples of European Orientalism, and has influenced the designs of other architects. The Orient Express was the name of a long-distance passenger train service originally operated by the *Compagnie Internationale des Wagons-Lits*. The route passed through Strasbourg, Karlsruhe, Stuttgart, Ulm, and Munich in Germany, Vienna in Austria, Budapest in Hungary, Bucharest in Romania, Rousse and Varna in Bulgaria and ending in Sirkeci.

4e299372-2148-578c-ac70-4b781a5ad8ce.name: *The First Train in Spain: Inaugurated 28 October 1848*
4e299372-2148-578c-ac70-4b781a5ad8ce.description: The railway connecting Barcelona and Mataró was the first one to be inaugurated in Spain. This train connected two important industrial hubs of Catalonia, as an example of the industrial development of this area in the middle of the 19th century.
4e299372-2148-578c-ac70-4b781a5ad8ce.author: Ana Cabrera
4e299372-2148-578c-ac70-4b781a5ad8ce.third_name: *Primer ferrocarril de España, inaugurado en el 28 de Octubre de 1848*

51be354a-b339-5d93-8690-4f26618ea9fb.name: Tramway
51be354a-b339-5d93-8690-4f26618ea9fb.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
51be354a-b339-5d93-8690-4f26618ea9fb.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
51be354a-b339-5d93-8690-4f26618ea9fb.description2: This railway carraige from the French Bône-Guelma company inaugurated, in April 1879, the opening of the first section of a 100 km long line which connected Tunis to Algeria. In 1800 it also acquired the Tuni-Sousse and Tunis-Bizerte lines, and thus gained a monopoly over the construction of railway lines in Tunisia, while the Italians bought the small Tunis-La Goulette-La Marsa (TGM) railway track.

51c01d82-0b4a-5399-8607-c519021252c0.name: Switchboard (*Telefon Santrali*)
51c01d82-0b4a-5399-8607-c519021252c0.keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication
51c01d82-0b4a-5399-8607-c519021252c0.description2: In 1840, the Ministry of Post made an announcement describing the postal service, declaring it necessary in order to facilitate communication among people. The first regulations about the postal organisation were taken from French Law in 1840. Ottoman Postal Code included 44 specific headlines. In 1855 the first telegraph service and in 1909 the first telephone service were put into common use as a demonstration of modern communication. In order to improve the technology of the telegraph systems, Ottoman authorities imported well-known machines with trademarks such as Siemens & Halske and Western Electric. As a result of this technological improvement, Ottoman officials decided to establish a telegraph factory. Between 1869 and 1915 this factory produced many devices and accessories.

51d89765-459f-5a2f-89bb-b09f35a3e9d2.name: Firman issued by Sultan Abdülmecid for the construction of the Constanţa–Cernavodă railway
51d89765-459f-5a2f-89bb-b09f35a3e9d2.description2: The first railway in the European part of the Ottoman Empire was built in Dobruja. Its construction was leased by the Ottoman sultan to the British company "Danube and Black Sea Railway and Kustendge harbour". According to the contract signed on 1 September 1857 the company had to build a railway linking the cities Constanţa and Cernavodă and could exploit it for 99 years, after which it became property of the Ottoman Empire. The railway, inaugurated on 4 October 1860, was 66 km long and was destined for freight transportation. After Dobruja was annexed by Romania in 1878, the state bought the railway from the British company (1882). Later, in order to connect it to the Romanian railway system (since Dobruja is separated from the rest of Romania by the Danube) a railway bridge was built across the Danube.

52e912d6-db07-5f7b-a1e2-6593559e25f6.name: Illustrated guide and timetable for travelling in the Orient. Featuring description of Constantinople and the most important cities in Turkey, Egypt, Greece, etc.
52e912d6-db07-5f7b-a1e2-6593559e25f6.description2: The growth of tourism entailed the production of travel guides, such as this one, which gave the potential tourist advice for travelling in "the Orient" - here meaning Greece, Turkey and Egypt.  This page provides a timetable for steam boats with timings which coincide with the international train lines, such as the Orient Express.

532b4aae-3420-5fef-ba89-4653325f00d7.name: *A young and an old Turk*
532b4aae-3420-5fef-ba89-4653325f00d7.description2: Carol Popp de Szathmari was born in Transylvania, but later settled in Bucharest, Wallachia, where he worked as court painter of princes Alexandru Dimitrie Ghica, Gheorghe Bibescu and Alexandru Ioan Cuza. During the reign of prince Carol of Hohenzollern, he was also court photographer. He is the author of five photographic albums with images of people and places from Bucharest and other regions in Romania, among which there are depictions of people belonging to the ethnic minorities of Romania, such as the Turks. He travelled twice to Istanbul, in 1860 and 1864, as member of prince Alexandru Ioan Cuza’s suite. During the Crimean War (1854-1855) he photographed the Russian and Turkish armies that occupied Wallachia and then went to Crimea, where he took more than 200 photos of the fights.

5476b9e7-1d62-5f52-a389-4e2da362bb9c.name: Skeleton telephone
5476b9e7-1d62-5f52-a389-4e2da362bb9c.description: The phone’s manual states that the Skeleton model was one of the first telephonic devices to be used in Morocco.
5476b9e7-1d62-5f52-a389-4e2da362bb9c.keywords: Telephone; technical innovations; communication; telephone network

5483dab5-d84f-5427-be2a-f5641e4aecc1.name: Monthly revenues deriving from the traffic of boats through the Suez Canal sent by the consul of the Austro-Hungarian Empire in Port Said (Egypt) to the Commodities Exchange of Trieste
5483dab5-d84f-5427-be2a-f5641e4aecc1.author: Chiara Artico
5483dab5-d84f-5427-be2a-f5641e4aecc1.archival: ASTS, Deputazione di Borsa poi Camera di commercio di Trieste, b. 92, fasc. 1222.
5483dab5-d84f-5427-be2a-f5641e4aecc1.third_name: *Compagnie Universelle du Canal Maritime de Suez, Mouvement recettes, Septembre 1876.*
5483dab5-d84f-5427-be2a-f5641e4aecc1.description2: Out of the 109 boats that had passed through the Canal in that month, 78 were from Britain, 8 from France, 7 from the Netherlands and the remaining 16 were from Spain, Germany, Italy, Austria, Denmark and Norway. British ships passed through the Suez Canal on their way to India and to other British colonial possessions.

5514d06c-0d42-5cd5-ad41-d94d1fe042aa.name: Photograph of a *Rakkas* (runner) in front of a Post Office
5514d06c-0d42-5cd5-ad41-d94d1fe042aa.description: The photograph is of a Moroccan *Rakkas* (runner or messenger), responsible for taking and bringing back official messages and mail.
5514d06c-0d42-5cd5-ad41-d94d1fe042aa.keywords: Postal office; Spanish protectorate; rakkas; postal system; delivery; magazine

579a1e8e-d0d1-5139-bb97-214a66f11b68.name: The Ottoman Navy, Mahmudiye
579a1e8e-d0d1-5139-bb97-214a66f11b68.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
579a1e8e-d0d1-5139-bb97-214a66f11b68.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; Ottoman navy; Mahmudiye
579a1e8e-d0d1-5139-bb97-214a66f11b68.description2: The 19th century saw further decline in Ottoman naval power, despite occasional recovery. Following the defeat against the combined British-French-Russian fleet at the Battle of Navarino in 1827, Sultan Mahmud II gave priority to developing a strong and modern Ottoman naval force. The first steam ships of the Ottoman Navy were acquired in 1828. The ship of the line Mahmudiye, which had 128 cannons on three decks and carried 1,280 sailors on board, was built for the Ottoman Navy at the Imperial Naval Arsenal (Tersâne-i Âmire) on the Golden Horn in Constantinople.

58a491a4-71cc-5b24-a1a9-764a71488439.name: *Works for the opening of the Corinth Canal*
58a491a4-71cc-5b24-a1a9-764a71488439.author: Maria Dimitriadou
58a491a4-71cc-5b24-a1a9-764a71488439.description2:
The Corinth Canal being dug. Photographer unknown.  
The Corinth Canal separates the Peloponnesian peninsula from the Greek. The idea of the canal was revived after Greece gained independence but soon abandoned due to economical reasons. The opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 gave an new impetus and the following year, the Zaimis government passed a law authorising the construction of the canal, which was formally inaugurated on 23 April 1882. Zaimis assigned the project to the Hungarian István Türr who set up the Société Internationale du Canal Maritime de Corinthe but the company failed and the project was finished by the company of Andeas Syngros. The canal was designed by the Hungarian engineer Béla Gerster with the assistance of the French Vincent Dauzants, a chief engineer of the Suez canal.

58b9817a-c39c-5ed0-9922-32e3e0ccbd6a.name: The bronze statue representing 22 countries of member of Universal Postal Union
58b9817a-c39c-5ed0-9922-32e3e0ccbd6a.description2: The Universal Postal Union was created in 1874, initially under the name "General Postal Union", as a result of the Treaty of Bern signed on 9 October 1874. The UPU is a specialized agency of the United Nations that coordinates postal policies among member nations, in addition to the worldwide postal system. Transportation freedom is guaranteed with this treaty.

59c09c6e-e0cc-5963-83cc-fd6b4aea8244.name: Bakırköy Railway Station
59c09c6e-e0cc-5963-83cc-fd6b4aea8244.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
59c09c6e-e0cc-5963-83cc-fd6b4aea8244.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph The Hijaz Railways
59c09c6e-e0cc-5963-83cc-fd6b4aea8244.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

59c2a789-38b6-526c-8c2e-10450f77128f.name: Long Moorish musket
59c2a789-38b6-526c-8c2e-10450f77128f.description: This musket, along with other pieces, was taken by Salvador de Foronda, a member of the Spanish Army, awarded for his actions in battle. He was a relative of the Marquis of Cerralbo and donated to his uncle’s museum these exceptional pieces in 1918. The Moorish musket, a long firearm that could be shot with a single arm while riding the horse, was described by Salvador as “one of the most ancient and authentic", a truly beauty with damascene work, romantically infused with the testimony of the war.
59c2a789-38b6-526c-8c2e-10450f77128f.author: Cecilia Casas Desantes
59c2a789-38b6-526c-8c2e-10450f77128f.materials: Wood, metal, fabric; handmade, damascene work

59eb8eb8-862f-5124-b1c8-abb0f2db5588.name: Hydrographic map of Lower Egypt and part of the Suez isthmus, engraved at the Dépôt de la Guerre
59eb8eb8-862f-5124-b1c8-abb0f2db5588.artist: Louis Maurice Adolphe Linant de Bellefonds
59eb8eb8-862f-5124-b1c8-abb0f2db5588.second_name: Drawn according to the work of M. Linant de Bellefonds, reviewed and completed in 1882 for the railways and the Suez canal. 1:250,000
59eb8eb8-862f-5124-b1c8-abb0f2db5588.description2: Louis Maurice Adolphe Linant de Bellefonds (1798–1883), artist and explorer passionate about Egypt, played a key role alongside Ferdinand de Lesseps in drawing and constructing the Suez Canal. He was given the title 'Bey' by the Egyptian viceroy, appointed director of Egyptian public works, and contributed to the irrigation of farmland. The map drawn in 1855 included the barriers; the outline of the Suez Canal and the railways were added in 1882.

5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.name: Barbadinhos steam pumping station at the time of its inauguration
5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.holder: Historical Archive, Empresa Portuguesa das Águas Livres (Portuguese Water Company)
5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.dimensions: Rectangular shape; length: 26 cm, width: 18 cm. Mounted on cardboard (30,5 x 24,5 cm)
5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.author: AHEPAL–EPAL’s Historical Archive
5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.keywords: Lisbon; water supply; Innovation; Industrial Archeology
5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.second_name: Central Pumping Station of Barbadinhos, machines storehouse, main or south façade
5aee46c9-4c7b-55fb-bca1-375579387666.description2: This picture is part of an album entitled "Canal Alviela / Inauguration / 3 October 1880" that includes 10 photographs by Francesco Rocchini. The picture depicts the main façade of the Barbadinhos steam pumping station at the time of its inauguration. The chimney and the engine room of the water reservoir of Barbadinhos can be seen on the right side of the picture. The steam station was in operation until 1928, when a new electrically powered station was opened. After decommissioning, the machines were not dismantled and are currently preserved. The building of the Barbadinhos steam pumping station houses the Water Museum (opened in 1987) and was classified in 2010 as a building of public interest.

5b43be53-1e86-5b15-9cc1-477c08fb7fbb.name: Official Bulletin establishing the Post, Telegraph and Telephone Office (PTT.)
5b43be53-1e86-5b15-9cc1-477c08fb7fbb.description: An Official Bulletin, signed by the Sultan of Morocco Mulay Yusuf ibn al-Hasan I, which concerns the creation of the Post, Telegraph and Telephone Office. The establishment of this Office was part of an agreement between Morocco and the French authorities, to promote the telecommunications sector, and put a stop to attempts by Britain and Spain to capitalise from it. The text defined the functions and services of the Office and its organisation. After independence, the Office became the Ministry (*Makhzen*) of Post, Telegraph and Telephone.
5b43be53-1e86-5b15-9cc1-477c08fb7fbb.holder: National Library of the Kingdom of Morocco
5b43be53-1e86-5b15-9cc1-477c08fb7fbb.keywords: Postal service; post offices; Moroccan postal service; communication; routes; rakkas; delivery; French in Morocco; protectorate; postal network

5b74420d-61f0-5db6-8b22-107ce274c47e.name: The Train Station from Anatolia
5b74420d-61f0-5db6-8b22-107ce274c47e.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
5b74420d-61f0-5db6-8b22-107ce274c47e.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Anatolian Railways
5b74420d-61f0-5db6-8b22-107ce274c47e.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

5bdaed42-778f-5c44-bbc4-20cefe2c165b.name: Retaining wall of the reservoir in Shellal, Egypt
5bdaed42-778f-5c44-bbc4-20cefe2c165b.author: Patrizia Pampana
5bdaed42-778f-5c44-bbc4-20cefe2c165b.second_name: The retaining wall of the first dam on the Nile
5bdaed42-778f-5c44-bbc4-20cefe2c165b.description2: In the year 1900, Count Giulio d’Aspremont, an Italian diplomat, visited the construction site of the first dam across the Nile (today known as the Aswan Low Dam or Old Aswan Dam). He took several photographs of the works and of the monuments on the island of Philae that were slated to be submerged by the water. He published some of them in the *Bulletin of the Italian Geographical Society*, where he wrote that up to 2,000 Italian workers were employed in the works (as stone-cutters, miners and masons), out of a total labour force of about 10,000 or 12,000; an Italian village had sprung up on the Nile banks, with modest little houses, trattorias and shops.

5bdb7155-07a2-5eb8-97fb-cb481391296f.name: A photo of the Dairy Laboratory at Fu`ad Agricultural Museum
5bdb7155-07a2-5eb8-97fb-cb481391296f.dates: 16 January 1938 (Photo taken during the inauguration of the museum)
5bdb7155-07a2-5eb8-97fb-cb481391296f.description2: The Fu`ad Agriculture Museum was considered the first of its kind in the Middle East and the Arab World during the 1930s. It was inaugurated during the time of King Faruq, the son of King Fu`ad, and houses a large number of collections related to agricultural and rural environments, as well as agricultural plants and animals.

5d9c0ecc-1cda-5806-b890-7ae8e461a596.name: Postal stamp
5d9c0ecc-1cda-5806-b890-7ae8e461a596.description: The Moroccan Telegraph Company, which had been responsible for the national post since 1911, started issuing stamps mainly to secure mail and parcels under the name of the “Management of the Chérifienne Post, Telegraph and Telephone”. This means that the first Moroccan stamp was issued on 22 May 1912.
5d9c0ecc-1cda-5806-b890-7ae8e461a596.keywords: Stamp; postal service; Spanish portectorate; French protectorate; technical innovation; celebration of progress; communication; railways; industrial railways

5e4318a5-d6ea-59f6-b209-38ea0cff4654.name: Postal map
5e4318a5-d6ea-59f6-b209-38ea0cff4654.keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication
5e4318a5-d6ea-59f6-b209-38ea0cff4654.description2: The network of routes for sending messages and transporting troops and supplies was carried out with a relay system, established in the 16th century in the Ottoman Empire. The messengers, who conveyed dispatches throughout the country, were identified as the Tatars. Private or personal correspondence was not a part of that relay system; it was built to fulfil governmental needs. Because of this reason the *reaya* (public) created an alternative postal method by using caravans, pilgrims, and private couriers called *ulaks*. The *Tanzimat* Decree, which was the declaration of process included reformation, modernization and westernization in 1839, proved that the Ottoman Empire was focused on its policy of changing governing to be more like modern Western European-style administrative practices.

5f76f108-6ffb-5c2b-8fe2-0ec05a6fae48.name: Various hydraulic machines used in Egypt to water the land. The first method is constructed in a linear manner and provides the land with water whenever it is in need. Part of "Dyke A"
5f76f108-6ffb-5c2b-8fe2-0ec05a6fae48.second_name: Illustrations taken from *Voyage d'Egypte et de Nubie*
5f76f108-6ffb-5c2b-8fe2-0ec05a6fae48.description2: The captain of the Danish Royal Marines Fréderic-Louis Norden (1708–1742) was sent to Egypt to draw monuments. His collection, *Voyage d’Égypte et de Nubie*, was published posthumously in 1755, and was added to in 1795 by the inclusion of scientific commentaries by Louis Langlès (1763–1824), founder of the École Spéciale des Langues Orientales and curator of oriental manuscripts at the Bibliothèque Impériale. This new edition, a product of Europen "Egyptomania", introduced some splendid new illustrations. In this particular page, the artist has focused on traditional hydraulic machinery.

61c3f6f4-ae5b-5188-a071-b1ffe734cb27.name: Messageries Maritimes's Istanbul-themed posters
61c3f6f4-ae5b-5188-a071-b1ffe734cb27.description2: *Messageries maritimes* was a French merchant shipping company. When it began, it operated on routes to the Middle East. Its ships were used as troop transports during the Crimean War, and were so helpful for the army that the Emperor gave the company the right to operate on the Bordeaux-Brazil route as thanks. This was the first French transatlantic line equipped with steamers. The following year, the *Société générale maritime* (later called *Compagnie générale transatlantique*) received the North Atlantic lines. From 1871 to 1914 the shipping company, now called *Compagnie des messageries maritimes*, saw its Golden Age.

61eb1293-6209-599c-bd83-34f180e3bec2.name: *The Port of Constanţa*
61eb1293-6209-599c-bd83-34f180e3bec2.description2: The Black Sea port of Constanța underwent its first modernization while Dobruja, the province where it is situated, was under Ottoman control. In 1857, when the Ottoman government hired a British company to build a railway in Dobruja, the concluded contract also stipulated the reconstruction of the Constanța port. Completed in 1864, it was still a small harbor with a wooden dock, a dam and one cereals depot. After Dobruja was annexed by Romania, a law was issued in 1885 for the “improvement and augmentation” of the port. In 1896 its modernization was leased to a French enterprise but due to some disagreements, three years later the state took over the works, which were led by architect Anghel Saligny. Inaugurated in 1909, the new port had 3 dams, several docks, depots, silos, an oil basin, an electric plant.

640180dd-059b-54fe-a33c-0700c3dd70f8.name: Photograph of the Beirut–Aleppo railway
640180dd-059b-54fe-a33c-0700c3dd70f8.author: Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
640180dd-059b-54fe-a33c-0700c3dd70f8.keywords: Transport; Railway; Communication; Connection; Innovation; Aleppo; Lebanon
640180dd-059b-54fe-a33c-0700c3dd70f8.description2: The second railway built in Lebanon opened in 1906 and ran from Beirut to Aleppo in present-day Syria. It connected with the first railway line at Riyaq. The connection between Aleppo and Beirut, a well-equipped and sizeable port, decreased trade in Alexandretta, the traditional port for merchandise leaving or entering Syria. Alexandretta was not connected to Aleppo by rail until 1914. Aleppo and Northern Syria became increasingly important as links between Damascus and Beirut were consolidated. This also marked the increasing importance of Beirut as a powerful city in the region and not only as a Mediterranean port.

64c7bc97-7cc3-58be-9d17-18bd4395053c.name: Map of Beirut's water networks
64c7bc97-7cc3-58be-9d17-18bd4395053c.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Rita El Hachem
64c7bc97-7cc3-58be-9d17-18bd4395053c.description2: This map shows the water networks around Lebanon, set up by the Ottoman government.

65d5d950-d069-5d9e-989f-ca9b3eb57b29.name: *Harem*
65d5d950-d069-5d9e-989f-ca9b3eb57b29.description2: Pascal Sébah (1823–1886) was a French photographer working in the Ottoman Empire. This photo of a harem is interesting insofar as it  differs from the mainstream representations of harems in the Western imagination, which were influenced by the painter Gérôme. Indeed, many local customs - both real and imagined - captured the interest of European artists, and their Orientalist art then fuelled both the Western fascination with and revulsion towards the East.

661636db-2ce1-5462-80af-0f6986d618f3.name: Railway station
661636db-2ce1-5462-80af-0f6986d618f3.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
661636db-2ce1-5462-80af-0f6986d618f3.history: The establishment of the French Protectorate in Tunisia (12 May 1881) quickly led to the introduction of a railway network throughout the country, to support civilian control in the areas where the Europeans had settled. The Grombalia station is an example of one of the new public buildings. This region has always occupied an important strategic position on the communication routes from North to South Tunisia, and its temperate climate and fertile lands made it home to an important wine-producing centre and European settlement, particularly for the Italians and the French.
661636db-2ce1-5462-80af-0f6986d618f3.description2: Designed by the French government during the colonial era as a building for public use, the Grombalia rail station is a rectangular building of around 100 m2 with no architectural features of note. The station is on the ground floor, which contains a shop, ticket office, and waiting room. The first floor was used for the stationmaster's accommodation. Its double-sloped roof is covered in red tiles, and the blue painting around the large windows are juxtaposed with the white façade. The Grombalia station is still in use today.

670372b2-f67e-5ac4-8b1b-28c10cd4bd8e.name: Section of a rail from Hijaz Railway with commemorative inscription
670372b2-f67e-5ac4-8b1b-28c10cd4bd8e.description: In September 1900, Sultan Abdul Hamid addressed a call for all Muslims all over the world to collect donations to establish a railway between Damascus and the holy places to facilitate transporting the pilgrims. The call was responded to enthusiastically and with the great support of all Muslims. The cost of the project was estimated at approximately five million Ottoman golden lira which were provided from: donations, the revenues of the Ottoman State earned from the sale of the stamps, and a special tax upon all the citizens for the railway. Construction of the narrow-gauge track (105cm) whose axle weight was (10.5 tonnes) began in 1900 with a wire telegraph line along its side connecting Damascus with Medina across Amman with a total track length of 1303km. The construction of the project ended in 1908. All the tracks and the stations were completed as detailed below: Mezerib Dera'a section, September 1901; Dera'a Al-Zarqa section, September 1902; Al-Zarqa Amman section, September 1903; Amman Ma'an section, September 1904; Ma'an Tabuk section, end of 1906; Tabuk Medain Saleh, September 1907; Medain Saleh Medina, September 1908. These rails were brought from the destroyed railroad tracks that were harmed by Arab revolt army attacks in 1917. On one side of the first rail is an Arabic phrase written in divan script: "*min khayrat mawlana Amir al-mu'minin al-sultan al-ghazi 'abdal-hamid khan thani 'azza nasruhu*".

6755e6c3-6bcf-5ff8-9576-394e0f98a7c5.name: Beginning of the Royal Road from the direction of the Fayum Directorate
6755e6c3-6bcf-5ff8-9576-394e0f98a7c5.keywords: King Fu`ad; Fayum Directorate; new roads; The Royal Road
6755e6c3-6bcf-5ff8-9576-394e0f98a7c5.description2: The beginning of the royal road from the Fayum Directorate during King Fu`ad I’s visit to the Directorate on 8 May 1927. Fu`ad I ruled Egypt from 9 October 1917 to 28 April 1936. During his reign, the 1919 revolution began, and the British had to end Egypt's status as a protectorate and declare it an independent country with sovereignty. Independence was declared on 15 March 1922. Also during his reign, the first public ministry was established in January 1924, headed by Sa`d Zaghlul. King Fu`ad had a number of important accomplishments, and for this reason this photo was chosen – to manifest King Fu`ad's concern with roads, especially the royal road towards the Fayum Directorate.

678d0b51-8dc7-59f3-818b-402d1bec24d6.name: *The Barrage or Nile dam*
678d0b51-8dc7-59f3-818b-402d1bec24d6.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
678d0b51-8dc7-59f3-818b-402d1bec24d6.archival: Smith, James - Minister of St. George's-in-the-West Parish, Aberdeen, *A Pilgrimage to Egypt: an account of a visit to Lower Egypt ... With ... Illustrations*, Aberdeen: J. Avery & Co., 1897, p. 261
678d0b51-8dc7-59f3-818b-402d1bec24d6.keywords: Pilgrimage; Christian pilgrimage; travel; travel book; Egypt; Nile; inventions; dams; irrigation; flood; agriculture; economy; French in Egypt
678d0b51-8dc7-59f3-818b-402d1bec24d6.description2: This picture, from the book *A Pilgrimage to Egypt: An Account of a Visit to Lower Egypt*, shows the Delta Barrage dam built by the French engineer Mougelle during the reign of Muhammad 'Ali Pasha to maintain the Nile water at a balanced level all the year. The barrage also served as a fortification against attack on Cairo or Upper Egypt. It consisted of a double bridge, the eastern part spanning the Damietta branch of the Nile, the western the Rosetta, with the head of the Delta between the two. The barrage had to be improved from 1883 by Sir Colin Scott Moncrief to solve structural problems with the foundations and the gates of the dam. The barrage and other dams testify to the importance of these structures to provide the water needed for irrigation in Egypt since antiquity.

67cb161d-180b-5b1b-8420-3bf9a2f55271.name: *The Algiers-Oran line*
67cb161d-180b-5b1b-8420-3bf9a2f55271.author: Dalila Orfali
67cb161d-180b-5b1b-8420-3bf9a2f55271.second_name: Taken from the publication *Algérie Comique et Pittoresque*
67cb161d-180b-5b1b-8420-3bf9a2f55271.description2: This illustration, from around 1860 in a local Oran publication in the west of Algeria, *L’Algérie Comique et Pittoresque*, comments on current affairs with a distinctively Mediterranean style and sense of humour. Salomon Assus, the father of the famous painter from the Algerian school Armand Assus, was one of the newspaper's first cartoonists.

68e8b7c1-4b26-5650-8465-4d55145c3d6c.name: *Convoy of pilgrims*
68e8b7c1-4b26-5650-8465-4d55145c3d6c.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
68e8b7c1-4b26-5650-8465-4d55145c3d6c.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph pilgrims; pilgrimage; travelling
68e8b7c1-4b26-5650-8465-4d55145c3d6c.description2: The Hijaz Railway was a narrow-gauge railway (1,050mm/​3ft, 5 11⁄32 in track gauge) that ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. It got no further than Medina, 400 kilometres (250mi) short of Mecca, due to the construction interruption caused by the outbreak of World War I. The main purpose of the railway was to establish a connection between Constantinople, the capital of the Ottoman Empire and the seat of the Islamic Caliphate, and Hijaz in Arabia, the site of the holiest shrines of Islam and the holy city of Mecca, the destination of the Hajj (annual pilgrimage).

68fae760-47a2-58aa-986f-28473ca5d989.name: Revolver
68fae760-47a2-58aa-986f-28473ca5d989.description: Leopold Gasser Austrian navy revolver produced between 1870 and 1919. Serial number 156122 engraved on the frame and on the smooth surface of the cylinder. On the left side of the revolver, the plate at the base barrel has an inscription: "PATENT RAST & GASSER WIEN 171290 GUSS STAHL". On the frame right under the cylinder serial number 156122 and to the left of it an apple pierced with an arrow and L. G. with the word "MARKE" was engraved. The revolver is fitted with chequered wooden grips fixed to the frame by a screw within an oval with ears of steel insert pressed into the wood of the grip plates. On the right side of the revolver an illegible marking was stamped with two Arabic letters ا ح under the marking. The letters are obviously initials of either the maker or the owner. The same initials in Arabic letters were engraved on the cylinder. At the top of the barrel a crown with two letters NI was engraved.

6c348586-1356-5ba4-b2b5-0c09d19282dc.name: The Victims of Labour
6c348586-1356-5ba4-b2b5-0c09d19282dc.author: Marina Minozzi
6c348586-1356-5ba4-b2b5-0c09d19282dc.keywords: Sculpture; Italian sculptors; realism; Verismo; social topics; post-unitarian Italian society; rights of workers; working class; life expectancy; poverty; industry; communication; industrial development; road; railway; international; universal exposition
6c348586-1356-5ba4-b2b5-0c09d19282dc.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
6c348586-1356-5ba4-b2b5-0c09d19282dc.description2: Vincenzo Vela studied at the academy of Fine arts of Brera and at the age of 22 he won an Academy of Venice competition. The artwork is an homage to the workers who died during the construction of the Gotthard Tunnel between 1872-82, which had implemented new cost-lowering techniques that also caused numerous incidents and loss of life. Work conditions were very unhealthy: temperatures over 30 degrees, gas exhalations and no air shafts. Even the accommodations were unhealthy and dirty. When the workers went on strike for the inhumane conditions, police shot at protesters, killing four workers. The miners in *The Victims of Labour* are depicted carrying the body of a dying classmate on a stretcher out of the tunnel. A self-portrait of the sculptor is recognisable in the classmate’s face. The harsh modelling of the workers’ bodies, almost deformed, makes the scene even more powerful. The artist affirmed he had no commission for this work which was a passion project. In 1895 it was cast in bronze on request of the Ministry of Education; in 1900 it was sent to the Universal Exhibition in Paris.
