6c6bffc7-20e9-569d-88cc-50d1ea81c42a.description2: This station of the Hijaz Railway was established in 1907. It was smaller than Mada'in Salih Station. It contains four buildings, a water well, and a wind mill. The buildings were built by stone materials and roofed with red tiles.

6d1c8ebf-40bc-511a-925c-b1e167d60a3d.name: Memo on the profits of the Suez Canal Company
6d1c8ebf-40bc-511a-925c-b1e167d60a3d.keywords: Suez Canal; Profits of the Suez Canal; Future of the Suez Canal
6d1c8ebf-40bc-511a-925c-b1e167d60a3d.description2: An important memo on the profits of the Suez Canal. It shows that the increase in average load during the last 25 years is met with an increase in net profits which are estimated to be less than five Francs per ton, although the navigation fees were much more than that amount during the period stipulated in the document. This is due to the increase in company expenses, and the company’s decision to decrease navigation fees.

6fb5d317-b1c7-55c6-a5a1-452d17f4b70a.name: *10 cents an issue. Le Télégraphe. Morning Newspaper. Special connections with the whole world.*
6fb5d317-b1c7-55c6-a5a1-452d17f4b70a.description2: Claude Chappe's invention of optical telegraphy was a turning point in the development of telecommunications. Built high up (e.g. on a hill or a roof), the mechanism consisted of a pole with movable arms, visible from a distance, which transmitted a code. Telegraphy became a very popular mode of communication during times of war, and was adopted by the National Convention of the First Republic in 1793. Even Napoléon I, who had shut down the French telegraph lines for fear of political troubles, had them reopened and extended to Europe in order to fight the anti-French Coalition. Telegraphy was an increasingly used mode of communication in the 19th century.

718961a1-beb1-58c3-8832-5f8a278c1682.name: The young ladies of the telephones: a view of a Parisian telephone exchange
718961a1-beb1-58c3-8832-5f8a278c1682.description2: The French telephone network was not automated at the beginning of the 20th century. Young unmarried women were often employed to take paying members' calls, and connect them to their requested number.

729b315c-3fb9-575e-96d9-d9e48639cd90.name: Revolver
729b315c-3fb9-575e-96d9-d9e48639cd90.description: Revolver of Leopold Gasser (serial number 8106) used for land/terrestrial defence as opposed to the navy. It is also known as “Montenegrin” as it was used not only by the Austrian army but also by the army of Montenegro. The exterior was nickelled, but the nickel finish has mostly worn away leaving only traces on the barrel and the frame. The revolver is fitted with genuine ivory grips. The absence of any indication for Austria and the presence of the crown “R” might indicate to its production in Liege/Belgium.

72e135bf-f1d2-56f9-a08f-ae59b081701d.name: 'The War on Trial'
72e135bf-f1d2-56f9-a08f-ae59b081701d.author: Giulia Barrera
72e135bf-f1d2-56f9-a08f-ae59b081701d.archival: Giuseppe Scalarini, Il processo alla guerra (Milano: Soc. Anonima Editrice "Avanti!", 1913), pp. 5-6.
72e135bf-f1d2-56f9-a08f-ae59b081701d.second_name: Anticolonial booklet published by the Italian Socialist Party, against Italian colonial expansion in Libya
72e135bf-f1d2-56f9-a08f-ae59b081701d.description2:
This booklet describes an imaginary trial against Giovanni Giolitti, the Italian Prime Minister who directed the colonial conquest of Libya in 1911-12. The judge asks Giolitti:  
– ‘Why did you get into other people’s home?’  
– ‘In order to defend our interests.’  
– ‘Good! And what about the slaughtering of women and children, the massacre of elderly people, and the hanging of men?’  
– ‘You see, your excellence, we needed to uplift Italian prestige.’  
– ‘And what about the thefts, the burnings and the planes that bombed huts?’  
– ‘It was our civilising mission.’ "

75ba6380-c797-5b14-a144-d7546e1f3572.name: *Album de la Dobrudgea* by Anatol Magrin
75ba6380-c797-5b14-a144-d7546e1f3572.description2: In 1878 Anatole Magrin was appointed secretary of the French consul to Constanța and then became vice-consul and consul. He married a Romanian woman and eventually settled in Constanța. He was the owner of the first photo studio in the city and later became the official photographer of king Carol I, who decorated him with the Romanian order of the Crown. He is considered to be the first artist to take photographs of Dobruja, a province in the south-east of Romania which was restored to Romania in 1878, after more than three centuries of Ottoman domination. Magrin’s photo album dedicated to Dobruja contains 56 photos of landscapes and people, some of which depict Turkish and Tatar communities (the Tatars and Turks represent one of Dobruja’s main ethnic minorities).

76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.name: Photograph of the Old Railway Station in Skopje
76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.holder: Museum of the City of Skopje
76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.author: Zoja Bogdanovska, historian, Museum of the City of Skopje
76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.keywords: Railroad; railway; railway station; Ottoman Balkans
76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.third_name: Fotografija na starata zeleznichka stanica vo Skopje
76457a6e-00a0-52e0-a869-4eec84837b92.description2: The first railroad in Macedonia was the track running from Thessalonica via Skopje to Belgrade. Its construction was financed with foreign investments and began in 1871. The track to Skopje was finished in 1873. The Skopje-Mitrovica railway line was completed in 1878. In 1888, it was connected to Serbian railways at the border crossing Zibevche near Vranje.

7a241c8e-d68e-5a99-8f6d-768433eb938e.name: Map of the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia
7a241c8e-d68e-5a99-8f6d-768433eb938e.description2: This map of Lombardy-Venetia from 1827 shows postal routes and information concerning the costs of travelling with the post coaches.

7a6f5cad-f74c-5502-95b2-2068560418a6.name: The Port From The Galata Tower
7a6f5cad-f74c-5502-95b2-2068560418a6.keywords: Photograph; Old İstanbul Photograph; İstanbul; Abdullah Brothers
7a6f5cad-f74c-5502-95b2-2068560418a6.description2: Abdullah Brothers is the name given to three men of Armenian origin, Viçen (1820-1902), Hovsep Abdullahyan (1830-1908) and Kevork (1839-1918) who started the art of photography in Turkey. For 40 years they photographed the people of Istanbul, landscapes, various political and social events, and prepared albums of historical and cultural values, as well as monuments.

7d30a2cd-fc11-5624-b8c4-b8d92b2e5e38.name: Photograph of Tétouan Railway Station, platform
7d30a2cd-fc11-5624-b8c4-b8d92b2e5e38.description: Completion of the railway line that connected Tétouan with Ceuta relates closely to plans for the construction of the new Port of Ceuta. This photograph depicts Tétouan Railway Station in relation to construction of the port. It was the military engineers Captain Mario Pinto and First Lieutenant Levi Arsenio Jimenez Montera who first offered to draft plans for the new line between the two cities, a distance of nearly 1,435m, and managed to get the project approved by the Ministry of War. While some railway lines in Morocco were abandoned early, this one resisted closure until the dawn of independence. Evidence shows that the route thrived during the Protectorate era as it was one of main Spanish penetration axes to the North at the time.

7f9082fe-da75-56c9-8c44-bba718558f12.dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century
7f9082fe-da75-56c9-8c44-bba718558f12.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Pascal Sebah
7f9082fe-da75-56c9-8c44-bba718558f12.description2: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Pascal Sébah (1823-86) was a pioneer photographer who worked in Istanbul. Sébah opened a photography studio known as "El Chark " in Pera in 1857. The studio's most successful period started with the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873. Sébah formed a partnership with Joaillier Polycarpe in 1885. In 1899, the two partners bought Abdullah Frères's archives. For the Vienna Universal Exhibition in 1873, Pascal Sébah prepared *The Ottoman Clothing Album* to be exhibited at the Ottoman Stand.

8138d27f-0df1-5e19-884f-c3f2fabf66df.name: Istanbul Main Post Office Opening Ceremony
8138d27f-0df1-5e19-884f-c3f2fabf66df.artist: Photograph: author unknown; building: architect Vedat Tek, architect Muzaffer Bey
8138d27f-0df1-5e19-884f-c3f2fabf66df.keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication
8138d27f-0df1-5e19-884f-c3f2fabf66df.description2: The Istanbul Main Post Office is an office building for postal services located at the *Sirkeci* quarter of the faith district in Istanbul, Turkey. It was designed by architect Vedat Tek in the First Turkish National architectural style and was constructed between 1903 and 1909. (Vedat Tek was a notable Turkish architect, who has been one of the leading figures of the First Turkish National Architectural Movement. He studied at the *École Centrale Paris*, graduating with a degree in civil engineering before he got his further education in architecture at the *Ecole des Beaux Arts* in Paris.) The four-story building houses a post office, the *Sirkeci* Post Office, office space for regional administration and also since 2000 the Istanbul Postal Museum. It is Turkey's largest post office building.

826abea9-d0a5-5b38-9d39-fb3cd81ac626.name: The Şirket-i Hayriyye’s Excursion Steamship
826abea9-d0a5-5b38-9d39-fb3cd81ac626.description2: The Şirket-i Hayriyye was the name of a steam boat joint-stock company which carried passengers and cargo on the Bosporus from 1854 to 1945. The company was established with the approval of the Sultan Abdulmecid. The steam boats belonging to company were sent from European countries, primarily Britain. The first captains of this boats were almost all of Rûm origin. After the establishment of the Republic of Turkey, the company and its goods were purchased by the state.

830c2e47-9fe7-5cca-984a-d06b95466a30.name: *Sketches of Aden*
830c2e47-9fe7-5cca-984a-d06b95466a30.description: These drawings show Steamer Point, an early British settlement in Aden, and one early steamer. *Sketches of Aden* is an account by a British officer who settled in Aden in the first half of the 19th century. Published in Madras in 1848, the book offers a synthesis of the history, geography, people and costumes of that important British settlement on the route to India. Although influenced by 19th-century European stereotypes and by the impact of a new environment, the author describes vividly the political events leading to the British conquest of the port in 1839, the ancient legends and the main events in the local history of Aden, its towns, commerce, living conditions and the heterogeneous population living in Aden: the Arab, Somali, Jewish and Indian communities.

84d5ec45-7bab-5d25-96f2-a48ed1fe7a85.name: *Entrance to Damascus*
84d5ec45-7bab-5d25-96f2-a48ed1fe7a85.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
84d5ec45-7bab-5d25-96f2-a48ed1fe7a85.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
84d5ec45-7bab-5d25-96f2-a48ed1fe7a85.artist: W. H. McFarlane (after a drawing by Harry Fenn 1838 – 1911)
84d5ec45-7bab-5d25-96f2-a48ed1fe7a85.description2: This coloured engraving by W. H. McFarlane shows the entrance to Damascus by the new French-built road through the Merj, or meadow, west of the city. Most probably this is the carriage road that had been established between Beirut and Damascus in 1863, at a time when most other connecting arterties were mere mule paths. French firms also built railways and ports in Syria during the later 19th century. The Ottoman style building in the background on the right is the Tekkiye Mosque Complex, built on the banks of the Barada river at the orders of Suleiman the Magnificent between 1554-1560 and incorporating a mosque, accomodation, a soup kitchen and a hospice.

8590f3c9-9d8b-54dd-b2b2-fadea483c89c.name: *In the year 2000: The tennis lawn; the eaglet hunters; on the road to London (Pas-de-Calais)*
8590f3c9-9d8b-54dd-b2b2-fadea483c89c.keywords: Inventions; transports' technical challenges; cartoon; caricature
8590f3c9-9d8b-54dd-b2b2-fadea483c89c.description2: The many technological advances of the 19th century stimulated the imagination of contemporary artists. Here, the various possibilities the invention of wings would have offered man are imagined, such as games, fighting and simplified travel.

868c8876-a63c-5812-a3d6-8c1fbf7d0e19.name: *Panoramic view of the Isthmus of the Suez, tracing the canal between the two seas*
868c8876-a63c-5812-a3d6-8c1fbf7d0e19.artist: Louis Maurice Adolphe Linant de Bellefonds
868c8876-a63c-5812-a3d6-8c1fbf7d0e19.keywords: Suez canal; Egypt; Ferdinand de Lesseps
868c8876-a63c-5812-a3d6-8c1fbf7d0e19.description2: Between 1859 and 1869, the Compagnie Universelle du Canal Maritime de Suez built a canal joining the Red Sea to the Mediterranean, thus opening up a strategic trade route towards the Indian subcontinent. This panoramic image was drawn by Louis Maurice Adolphe Linant de Bellefonds (1798–1883), artist and explorer fascinated with Egypt who played a key role, alongside Ferdinand de Lesseps, in the planning and construction of the Suez Canal.

86959e1d-38a4-5f53-9007-4188fc788f51.name: Post card sent via *Poste-Cherifienne*
86959e1d-38a4-5f53-9007-4188fc788f51.description: A postcard dated 13 February 1920 sent via the postal service that connected the city of Tétouan, which was a city under the Spanish Protectorate, with the town of Kasr el-Kabir, which was on the border between the French and Spanish protectorates. On the postcard are two stamps of five cents and twenty-five cents. The front of the postcard shows a picture of a Moroccan *Rakkas* (runner or messenger).
86959e1d-38a4-5f53-9007-4188fc788f51.keywords: Postal office; Spanish protectorate; rakkas; postal system; delivery

869766dc-71ca-53a7-b67f-e1ed2b58d4ac.name: La Goulette
869766dc-71ca-53a7-b67f-e1ed2b58d4ac.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
869766dc-71ca-53a7-b67f-e1ed2b58d4ac.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
869766dc-71ca-53a7-b67f-e1ed2b58d4ac.description2: The expansion of the city of Tunis necessitated the construction of a large modern port which would be accessible to large-tonnage ships. Thus, in the early years of the French protectorate, the port of Tunis, La Goulette, saw a sharp increase in traffic. As well as a fishing port, the primary function of La Goulette, it also became an industrial centre thanks to the construction of a power plant on the north side of the canal, which served the tramways and the electric railway going to the northern suburbs. Finally, on the eve of the war, La Goulette had also become a residential town, particularly popular in summer for its seaside resorts.

87f34acd-b200-5f1a-b478-34b80e307ce2.name: Spanish Franciscan Church of Buenaventura
87f34acd-b200-5f1a-b478-34b80e307ce2.history: Built in 1890, the church closed in 1968 and remained abandoned until fairly recently. When restoration of the Old *Medina* began, the church was selected for renovation and now has exhibition and media spaces, a comprehensive library of over 6,000 titles and a discovery space for children.
87f34acd-b200-5f1a-b478-34b80e307ce2.keywords: Religious building; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic architecture in Morocco; Islamic influence; traditional building; traditional city; city; urban space; Islamic city; Islamic urban space; plan; urban planning; church; Spanish in Morocco; Moroccan city; Christians in Morocco; migration; work
87f34acd-b200-5f1a-b478-34b80e307ce2.description2: Built for the Spanish community based in Casablanca, this church stands in the Old *Medina* on land donated by Sultan Mulay al-Hasan I. The construction of this church testifies to the improving relationship between Morocco and Spain and highlights the importance of the Spanish community in Casablanca, which was very active in the port sector and played a dynamic role in the local and international economy.

894e770e-bdda-5d94-ae6c-90aaf47244ae.name: Beirut–Damascus Railway Company headquaters
894e770e-bdda-5d94-ae6c-90aaf47244ae.holder: Railway and Public Transportation Authority, Ministry of Transportation

894e770e-bdda-5d94-ae6c-90aaf47244ae.description2: This photograph shows the headquarters of Lebanon Railway Company in Beirut.

8a229227-3cb6-53ea-978a-a63f9f557d11.name: Patent for the invention of the fountain pen with a replaceable ink cartridge
8a229227-3cb6-53ea-978a-a63f9f557d11.description2: Pedagogue, engineer and mathematician Petrache Poenaru was the first Romanian inventor to obtain a patent. After 1821 he studied in Germany and then in France. While in Paris, he invented the fountain pen with a replaceable ink cartridge, a pen devised to ensure a constant flow of ink, preventing ink leaks, and to allow the replacement of some of the component parts. On 27 May 1827 the Manufactures Bureau within the French Ministry of Internal Affairs granted him for this invention a patent with a validity of five years. Although his invention did not become known at the time and was not commercially exploited, Poenaru is considered to be the first inventor to receive a patent for a fountain pen.

8b529731-afad-5c0e-8816-7664ae89852a.name: Lithographed Qur’an, originally written by Shukr Zadeh (d. AH 1166 / AD 1753)
8b529731-afad-5c0e-8816-7664ae89852a.holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
8b529731-afad-5c0e-8816-7664ae89852a.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
8b529731-afad-5c0e-8816-7664ae89852a.artist: Original calligraphed by Shukr Zadeh (d. AH 1166 / AD 1753)
8b529731-afad-5c0e-8816-7664ae89852a.description2: This Qur'an, originally caligraphed by the famous Ottoman calligrapher Shukr Zadeh is the first Qur'an to be printed in an Islamic country by way of lithograpy. It was produced around 1850 AD.While printing had begun in Europe many centuries ago, the Islamic world continued to favour handwritten books, and most certainly as regards copies of the Holy Qur’an. In 1834, the first edition of Gustav Fluegel’s printed Qur’an was published, while in the Ottoman Empire, the printing of Qur’ans began only in the second half of the 19th century, both in Egypt and in Istanbul. Most were lithographed, as they had the look and feel of manuscripts. Most importantly, all the required recitational signs could be rendered accurately.

8ba03860-993b-5dbf-9a66-b44cd6b52d86.name: Simplon-Orient Express Poster
8ba03860-993b-5dbf-9a66-b44cd6b52d86.description2: Roger Broders was a French illustrator and artist best known for his travel posters promoting tourism destinations in France. Broders' illustrations were distinctive for their simple lines and bold, flat areas of colour, combined with noticeable graphical perspective showing the featured mountains and seascapes in the background. Broders' illustrations depicting people show active, elongated figures wearing elegant, contemporary clothes. His posters were simply and boldly lettered identifying the destination, and were supplemented with a brief slogan.

8c2abbac-16e2-5805-a239-068b6318e25d.name: *Hüdavendigar* Newspaper
8c2abbac-16e2-5805-a239-068b6318e25d.description2: After the *Tanzimat* (reforms), newspapers in Arabic, Persian, Bulgarian, Serbian, Albanian, Kurdish, English, French, Italian and German began appearing in the Ottoman Empire. Some of them were bilingual as Turkish-Greek, Turkish-Armenian and Turkish-Arabic. *Hüdavendigar* was a provincial newspaper of Bursa and it was first published on 19 February 1869. The same year, starting with the 80th issue, the back page was printed in Armenian. The paper was published twice (Wednesday and Saturday) and then four times a week. It was 50 x 25cm. Subscription for a year was 100 kuruş, for six months was 50 kuruş and one issue was 20 para (1/2 kuruş). It continued to be published until 1953 under different names.

8dec350b-560d-5475-8a47-00b9dd25268c.name: Medal of Emperor Franz Joseph I
8dec350b-560d-5475-8a47-00b9dd25268c.keywords: Emperor Franz Joseph; Suez; Suez Canal; Egypt; numismatics
8dec350b-560d-5475-8a47-00b9dd25268c.description2: A medal depicting the symbolic figure of Egypt sitting on a sphinx. In the background, the three pyramids of Giza and a sailing ship can be seen. The opposite side of the medal has a portrait of Emperor Franz Joseph. The medal was created in commemoration of the opening of the Suez Canal in 1869.

8f55adc5-662c-55f8-a485-b18851210a66.name: Anatolian Railways
8f55adc5-662c-55f8-a485-b18851210a66.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
8f55adc5-662c-55f8-a485-b18851210a66.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Anatolian Railways
8f55adc5-662c-55f8-a485-b18851210a66.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

8f60990a-2e19-50e5-b91c-31a7c8a103fd.name: Beirut Port before expansion
8f60990a-2e19-50e5-b91c-31a7c8a103fd.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury, Hady El Hajj, Jennifer Harb, Cynthia Karaki
8f60990a-2e19-50e5-b91c-31a7c8a103fd.keywords: Commerce; Expansion; Economy; Trading; Goods; Transportation; Port; Harbor; Communication; Beirut
8f60990a-2e19-50e5-b91c-31a7c8a103fd.description2: This photograph shows the Beirut port before its expansion. The dam was built under the command of Ibrahim Pasha. This old port underwent several important changes in the late 19th century, including the construction of a commercial tribunal and expansion of the port. This expansion involved the enlargement of existing buildings and filling areas of sea with rock brought in along the Nahr al-Kalb railway.

908862b3-3d2c-5b16-93ce-f2a0873efd37.name: *Algiers port*
908862b3-3d2c-5b16-93ce-f2a0873efd37.author: Dalila Orfali
908862b3-3d2c-5b16-93ce-f2a0873efd37.description2: Albert Marquet spent 1904 and 1907 in the company of Fauve, and in 1913 he lived in Tangier with Matisse and Camoin. Seven years later in 1920 he visited Algiers for the first time, and went on to spent a few months there every year henceforth. He also lived in Algiers for the duration of the Second World War. Marquet was friendly with most of the artists from the Algerian school, and exhibited his paintings in galleries in the centre of town. Many of his paintings were on the theme of Algiers' harbour. In 1939, his friends from the Salle Bordes organised his first solo exhibition. His style, which was characterised by the luminosity and clarity he saw in North Africa, was an important early influence on the Algerian painter Mohamed Temam.

90aa72df-4823-5e48-bcc0-2aa150e3f718.name: *The Suez Canal*
90aa72df-4823-5e48-bcc0-2aa150e3f718.author: Marina Minozzi
90aa72df-4823-5e48-bcc0-2aa150e3f718.keywords: Waterway; Austria; Lloyd; Assicurazioni Generali; Bourse; Adriatic; Egypt; Said; Ismail; Pasha; Ferdinand de Lesseps; Suez Canal Company; Compagnie universelle du canal maritime de Suez; vice-president; route; India; International exhibition
90aa72df-4823-5e48-bcc0-2aa150e3f718.description2: Alberto Rieger studied at the Academy of Venice thanks to the patronage of the Baron Pasquale Revoltella, who commissioned him to create the painting showing the Suez Canal, which was presented at the Exposition of Fine Arts in 1864. The artwork is meant to celebrate the most important enterprise in Revoltella’s career; he personally travelled to Suez in 1861-62 to supervise the works for the construction of the channel that he promoted. The painting was executed by studying technical maps of the ground, sketches and photographs. The result is very close to the actual conditions of the city of Cairo, the pyramids and the delta of the Nile. The artist was commissioned also an open view of the city of Trieste by Pasquale Revoltella.

949e75ce-78cf-577e-95d9-461cc0734d07.name: *On the omnibus (or inside a tramway passing over a bridge)*
949e75ce-78cf-577e-95d9-461cc0734d07.description2: The question of multi-passenger transport emerged first in capital cities. In the 17th century, Blaise Pascal had the idea of creating transport lines in Paris with scheduled itineraries for horse-drawn carriages seating 8 people. This type of transport saw increasing success in the 19th century as did, on the other hand, the use of cabs with specific destinations. In 1855, all Parisian omnibus companies were merged into the "Compagnie Générale des Omnibus" at the request of the Chief Commissioner of the Seine, in a desire to prioritise the movement of tourists visiting the Exposition Universelle (world fair). Steam or fuel-powered tramways were also introduced in the 1870s. This drawing does not accurately reproduce the atmosphere of those overcrowded omnibuses, however, as Mary Cassat chose to foreground a mother who, lost in her thoughts, does not notice the nanny playing affectionately with her daughter.

9599bee6-4ecd-5e61-803d-f6a17fddee21.name: The Istanbul Main Post Office
9599bee6-4ecd-5e61-803d-f6a17fddee21.notice: This is an unedited Database entry and may contain errors and inconsistencies in spelling. 9599bee6-4ecd-5e61-803d-f6a17fddee21.history: The Istanbul Main Post Office is an office building for postal services located at Sirkeci quarter of Fatih district in Istanbul, Turkey. It was designed by architect Vedat Tek in First Turkish National architectural style and was constructed between 1903 and 1909. The four-story building houses a post office, the Sirkeci Post Office, office space for regional administration and also since 2000 the Istanbul Postal Museum. It is Turkey's largest post office building.

9825c289-5dc5-5c51-b115-fa920eda0b57.name: The artificial channel built at Shellal, during the construction of the first dam on the Nile
9825c289-5dc5-5c51-b115-fa920eda0b57.author: Patrizia Pampana
9825c289-5dc5-5c51-b115-fa920eda0b57.description2: In the year 1900, Count Giulio d’Aspremont, an Italian diplomat, visited the construction site of the first dam across the Nile (today known as the Aswan Low Dam or Old Aswan Dam). He took several photographs of the works and of the monuments on the island of Philae that were slated to be submerged by the water. He published some of them on the *Bulletin of the Italian Geographical Society*, where he wrote that up to 2,000 Italian workers were employed in the works (as stone-cutters, miners and masons), out of a total labour force of about 10,000 or 12,000; an Italian village had sprung up on the Nile banks, with modest little houses, trattorias and shops.

9a890b71-5d5a-57ef-b26d-c4592e54b5ac.name: Beirut Tramway station
9a890b71-5d5a-57ef-b26d-c4592e54b5ac.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Rita El Hachem
9a890b71-5d5a-57ef-b26d-c4592e54b5ac.description2: This photograph shows the main tramway station in Beirut, located on Corniche el Nahr Street by the river in the district of Burj Hammud. It was constructed in 1906 under the command of the Ottoman government, and housed the carts and the engineering station.

9c17568a-e2ca-5524-b5ae-c2d13aa4c2ac.name: The Beirut water factory
9c17568a-e2ca-5524-b5ae-c2d13aa4c2ac.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Rita El Hachem
9c17568a-e2ca-5524-b5ae-c2d13aa4c2ac.description2: Located in the suburb of Dbayeh, this factory provided the daily water supply for all of Beirut. The company was founded in 1873 and the factory was first opened in 1896. The water was taken from the Nahr al-Kalb river and distributed across a large water network.

9c2ac3c9-ddf9-5578-9e26-fad8ec3a615c.name: Dhow collection
9c2ac3c9-ddf9-5578-9e26-fad8ec3a615c.keywords: Boat; ship; dhow; pearling; fishing; trade; transportation
9c2ac3c9-ddf9-5578-9e26-fad8ec3a615c.description2: The National Museum of Qatar holds, in its collection, a fleet comprising of 14 dhows. The growing collection includes a variety of traditional dhows, with several models dating to the early 20th century, as well as more recent replicas of traditional vessels. Originating from Oman, Bahrayn, India and Qatar, among other places traditional dhows represented include *jalbut* (small to medium sized), *shuw\`i* (medium sized, once used for fishing and coastal trade), *sanbuq* (largest type in the Arabian Gulf today) and *baglah* (traditional, deep-sea dhows once used for the long – haul transport of goods.)

9dcd91c6-e5a8-5dd3-b2fb-aa1eefe94502.archival: *Visite au Canal maritime de Suez. Rapport sur l’entraprise de M. Ferdinand de Lesseps adressé à la Chambre de commerce d’Alger par M. Félix Desvignes délégué au Congrès commercial international de Suez*, Alger 1865.
9dcd91c6-e5a8-5dd3-b2fb-aa1eefe94502.description2: This map was printed four years before the opening of the Suez Canal, in a book published in Algiers by the local Chamber of Commerce. It is evidence of the interest that the opening of the Canal aroused in North African countries other than Egypt, because of the business opportunities that it created.

9ee00ba7-2731-5d14-b9bf-0d46da259600.name: Ismail, Khedive of Egypt (1830–1895)
9ee00ba7-2731-5d14-b9bf-0d46da259600.keywords: Ismail, Khedive of Egypt; Suez Channel; Great Britain
9ee00ba7-2731-5d14-b9bf-0d46da259600.description2: Portrait of Ismail, Khedive of Egypt (1830–1895), who financed the construction of the Suez Canal. Because of the enormous costs of the building and his reform measures, Egypt's debt rose from three million pounds sterling to 100 million pounds sterling. In 1875 Egypt was bankrupt and Ismail Pasha was forced to sell 176,602 shares to Great Britain for 3,976,582 pounds sterling. Egypt came under financial control of France and Great Britain.

9fa1fbea-a4e2-5d50-9509-67fa9073a9d8.name: Token
9fa1fbea-a4e2-5d50-9509-67fa9073a9d8.description2: Brass token issued by Borel Lavalley et Companie. In the centre is one of the sailing ships whose journey times would be dramatically improved by using the new Suez Canal.

a0e6366a-857a-5838-b99e-0c94fb227f54.name: Dhat Hajj Station
a0e6366a-857a-5838-b99e-0c94fb227f54.holder: Saudi Commission for Tourism and Antiquities
a0e6366a-857a-5838-b99e-0c94fb227f54.history: Dhat Hajj is one of the most famous historical monuments inTabuk region, located at the north of the region at a distance of 85 km close to the Saudi-Jordanian border. This was a village inhabited in previous eras, as experienced by the caravans of pilgrims for rest and water supply. The importance of the village was increased with the arrival of the Hijaz Railway.

a3cd6343-e399-52fc-beca-9b8315cf4639.name: *Panorama of the Compagnie Transatlantique* (French Line). *The "La Ville de Rome" steamer leaving the port of Algiers via Montenard*
a3cd6343-e399-52fc-beca-9b8315cf4639.artist: Photographer: Neurdein Frères; artist: Frédéric Montenard
a3cd6343-e399-52fc-beca-9b8315cf4639.second_name: Taken from the Exposition Universelle of 1889
a3cd6343-e399-52fc-beca-9b8315cf4639.description2: The emergence of steam boats in the 19th century allowed important maritime trade relationships to develop. In 1855, the Pereire brothers adopted this new method of transport and founded the Compagnie Générale Transatlantique (The French Line). The first line built served New York. In the 1880s the company then established an important line from Marseille to North Africa, which consisted of a 12-steamer strong fleet, the "sister ships" of the "Ville de Rome", which was first put into use in 1881. In March 1889, the "Ville de Rome" was run aground and washed up on the shores of Menorca. The passengers were evacuated in time, but the storm caused the wreck of the ship to break in two.

a5f9ccce-bdce-5ea9-8c27-06ad29d2353c.name: *Construction of a dam at Noisiel. State of the works on the 5th of August 1885*
a5f9ccce-bdce-5ea9-8c27-06ad29d2353c.artist: Photographer: Deraine and Auguste Hippolyte Collard
a5f9ccce-bdce-5ea9-8c27-06ad29d2353c.description2: Although little-known today, Auguste Hippolyte Collard (1812–1880s) contributed significantly to the rise of photography in France. He chose to specialise professionally in the photography of important construction sites. Thanks to him, today we can reconstruct the building of, for example, the Marne Dam at Noisiel in 1885. This dam is associated with the famous chocolatier Menier who became a pioneer in the field of cocoa refining, introducing the use of water power, among other new methods for the refinement of cocoa.

a63d4087-1cd4-5ec4-b4ee-b445f990556b.name: *Chargeurs réunis. French steam-travel company (with destinations in South America)*
a63d4087-1cd4-5ec4-b4ee-b445f990556b.description2: At the end of the 19th century, France tried to catch up with its counterparts in the arms trade, as it had begun to fall behind England, Germany and others in recent decades. Commercial interests also played a part. In 1872, the Compagnie des Chargeurs Réunis established a maritime relationship between France and South America for the movement of passengers and merchandise. As this poster shows, they put great emphasis on the different services passengers were provided aboard these steamers.

a946e99a-c0f3-5d45-9fb0-6eec1cfb9b75.name: The cutting of granite blocks for the construction of the first dam on the Nile. Many Italian stonecutters participated in the works
a946e99a-c0f3-5d45-9fb0-6eec1cfb9b75.author: Patrizia Pampana
a946e99a-c0f3-5d45-9fb0-6eec1cfb9b75.description2: In the year 1900, Count Giulio d’Aspremont (an Italian diplomat), visited the construction site of the first dam across the Nile (today known as the Aswan Low Dam or Old Aswan Dam). He took several photographs of the works and of the monuments on the island of Philae that were slate to be submerged by the water. He published some of them on the *Bulletin of the Italian Geographical Society*, where he wrote that up to 2,000 Italian workers were employed in the works (as stone-cutters, miners and masons), out of a total labour force of about 10,000 or 12,000; an Italian village had sprung up on the Nile banks, with modest little houses, trattorias and shops.

aba67976-e763-523c-b6b8-d3d8d4b775b6.name: Spread from lithographic-printed publication
aba67976-e763-523c-b6b8-d3d8d4b775b6.description: Despite Arabic lithographic printing arriving late to Morocco, the government did its best to catch up and printed a considerable number of books in all disciplines.
aba67976-e763-523c-b6b8-d3d8d4b775b6.keywords: Printing; lithograph; book; manuscript; social changes; technical innovation; literacy; illiteracy

acc57934-ae32-5e43-8f31-305447337577.name: Water pumping equipment in Kağıthane, Istanbul
acc57934-ae32-5e43-8f31-305447337577.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
acc57934-ae32-5e43-8f31-305447337577.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; History of Water in Ottoman Empire; Water Pump Station
acc57934-ae32-5e43-8f31-305447337577.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. Cendere Hamidian Water Pump Station was built by Abdülhamid II in 1902 at an altitude of 34 metres above sea level. With its function, architectural design and mechanical equipment, the station is a unique monument to the history of the architecture industry in the Ottoman Empire. It pumped to Balmumcu and Beşiktaş – in the direction of Tophane, moving water coming from 20 different pipes in Kağıthane using steam pump machines.

ad3c4a56-381f-553f-b5a5-133f25218054.name: A telegram from the Khedive of Egypt to the Ottoman sultan
ad3c4a56-381f-553f-b5a5-133f25218054.keywords: Ottoman Sultan; Khedive of Egypt; Telegrams
ad3c4a56-381f-553f-b5a5-133f25218054.description2: A telegram from the Khedive of Egypt to the Ottoman Sultan expressing his loyalty and best wishes on 15 December 1897.

b1761f2e-80b8-586f-b4e2-c3736d979725.name: Photograph of an employee outside the *Poste-Cherifienne* office
b1761f2e-80b8-586f-b4e2-c3736d979725.description: The first national post and transport service in Morocco was founded by Mulay al-Hasan I on 20 Jumada I 1390 (22 November 1892) and was known as the *Poste-Makhzen*. The office was established in order to take control nationally of the postal (mainly parcels and messengers) service in Morocco, but competition from private foreign firms was tough. When in 1892 the Sultan first gave orders for port managers to take control of Morocco’s interests in this regard, this nascent organisation included 13 Moroccan cities, defined as zones connected by transport links, and each defined by specific costs.
b1761f2e-80b8-586f-b4e2-c3736d979725.keywords: Postal service; post offices; Moroccan postal service; communication; routes; port; rakkas; delivery; local postal service; foreign companies; private firms; postal network

b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.name: Steam engine building
b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.holder: Prussian Palaces (Stiftung Preussische Schlösser und Gärten Berlin Brandenburg)
b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.history:
In October 1842 the steam engine in the "Mosque," which could reach 81.4 horsepower, was inaugurated, allowing jets of water from the great fountain in front of Sanssouci Palace to rise to an impressive 38 meters. By possessing what was the most powerful machine in Prussia at the time, built by the young entrepreneur August Borsig, King Frederick William IV hoped to compete with the technical supremacy of England.  
Although today's supply of water to the fountains in Sanssouci Park is provided by means of modern electrical pumps, a visit to the "Mosque" allows the visitor to experience a technical marvel from days past that is still in operation.
b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.keywords: Moorish style; Romanticism; Sanssouci; Potsdam; exoticism; steam engine; steam pumping; Frederick William IV; gardens
b1a53072-23dd-58c0-b8c4-495759373b61.description2: The Steam Engine Building, located on a bay of the Havel River called the Neustädter Havelbucht, is at once the most charming as well as the most exotic building in Potsdam. Frederick William IV, the "Romantic on the throne," had it built by Ludwig Persius from 1841-1843, "in the style of the Turkish mosques, with a minaret as a smokestack." The building, which could still be seen at that time from Sanssouci Palace, added a picturesque architectural accent to the Potsdam cultural landscape.

b1ada77d-4a0f-5105-a292-423509ecec6b.name: Haydarpaşa Train Station
b1ada77d-4a0f-5105-a292-423509ecec6b.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
b1ada77d-4a0f-5105-a292-423509ecec6b.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Ancient Istanbul; Train Station
b1ada77d-4a0f-5105-a292-423509ecec6b.description2: In 1871 Sultan Abdülaziz ordered a rail line to be built from Haydarpaşa to İzmit. Haydarpaşa station opened in 1872, and in 1888 the Anatolian Railway (CFOA) took over the line and the station. Since the station was built next to the Bosporus, freight trains would unload at Haydarpaşa and the freight would be transferred to ships. Haydarpaşa was chosen to be the northern terminus of the Baghdad Railway and the Hijaz Railway in 1904 and with rail traffic increasing, a new and larger building was required. The Anatolian Railway hired two German architects; Otto Ritter and Helmut Conu to build the new building. They chose a neo-classical structure and construction started in 1906.

b1caaa98-898d-5835-84d6-2569546ecf1d.name: Document attesting to the 'Telegraph Crisis' between Morocco and Great Britain
b1caaa98-898d-5835-84d6-2569546ecf1d.description: A letter from Sultan al-Hasan I to his Minister of Foreign Affairs and representative in Tangier, Muhammad ibn al-‘Arabi al-Torres, ordering the immediate cessation of work on installation of the telegraph system between Gibraltar and Tangier, which the British had undertaken without negotiating with Morocco, thereby causing a diplomatic crisis between the two countries.
b1caaa98-898d-5835-84d6-2569546ecf1d.keywords: Communication; technical innovation; telegraph; telegraph installation; Telegraph Crisis; foreign companies; British in Morocco; diplomacy; Moroccan-British relations

b1dc4de3-1a52-53d0-8dcb-4569af75ef27.description2: One of the Hijaz Railway stone bridges which was built in an area between Tabuk and al-'Ula to allow the train to cross the wadi in tadarees area.

b34a6459-d73e-575a-bf25-d6eeecca51a1.name: *The Opening of the Suez Canal*
b34a6459-d73e-575a-bf25-d6eeecca51a1.author: Marina Minozzi
b34a6459-d73e-575a-bf25-d6eeecca51a1.keywords: Sculptors; route; travel; waterway; Austria; Lloyd; Assicurazioni Generali; Bourse; Adriatic; Egypt; Said; Ismail; Pasha; Ferdinand de Lesseps; Suez Canal Company; Compagnie universelle du canal maritime de Suez; vice-president; Cairo; India
b34a6459-d73e-575a-bf25-d6eeecca51a1.description2: The artist Pietro Magni studied at the Academy of Brera, travelled to Rome in 1849 and battled for the Roman Republic. His first artwork as mentioned in the author’s biography is *The First Steps*, known though the photographs to have been on display at the International Exhibition in London in 1862. In 1863 the businessman Pietro Revoltella commissioned the artist to create a marble group showing the opening of the Suez Canal, now in the Revoltella Museum in Trieste. It shows how important the project was for the commissioner, confident that the new opening toward the East would offer economic advantages to his city. Unfortunately he died two months before seeing the Suez Canal completed. The sculpture shows a classical allegory with Europe uniting the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea, behind them the genius of commerce with winged feet indicating the canal the unifies Europe and Asia.

b4a14dd7-63bc-5f3a-b31a-2ae6a297fc74.name: Qatranah Railway Station
b4a14dd7-63bc-5f3a-b31a-2ae6a297fc74.author: Mohammad Najjar
b4a14dd7-63bc-5f3a-b31a-2ae6a297fc74.history: In 1900-1908, Sultan Abdul Hamid with the help and support of Germany established a Railway between Damascus and Mecca (1700 km) to facilitate transporting the pilgrims. The track from Medina to Mecca (400 km) was never realized. The cost of the project was estimated at approximately 5 million Ottoman golden liras, which were provided from: private donations, revenues of the Ottoman State from the sale of stamps, and a special tax upon all citizens for the railway. Construction of the narrow-gauge track (105cm) began in 1900 with a wire telegraph line along its side connecting Damascus with Medina across Amman with a total track length of 1303 km. Official inaugurations of the tracks and stations were scheduled to coincide with the accession of the Sultan to the throne in the month of September every year. The construction of the project ended in 1908.
b4a14dd7-63bc-5f3a-b31a-2ae6a297fc74.keywords: Hijaz; railway; station; pilgrimage; hajj; pilgrimage route; communication; telegraph; Jordan; Damascus; Mecca; Makka; Amman; Zarqa; Qatranah; Ma'an; Amman; Tabuk; Arabian Peninsula; Ottoman; Abd al Hamid; Germany; Meinsner
b4a14dd7-63bc-5f3a-b31a-2ae6a297fc74.description2: Qatranah is an important station on the Hijaz railway. It consists of a group of building along the railroad. The station had been protected by a renovated small 16th-century fortress located to the west of the railway. The fortress was provided with water wells and pools for both the humans and the animals. The various components of the project including the rails, steam engines, bridges, stations were an industrial, architectural and engineering statement that had a huge influence on Jordan. The tracks and the station was completed in September 1904.

b532b295-4380-5ea9-951e-1e3a7150eff2.name: The Central Asian railway. Proposal for a direct line from Europe to India.
b532b295-4380-5ea9-951e-1e3a7150eff2.description2: Charles Cotard was an engineer and graduate of the famous École Polytechnique who dedicated his life to developing new transports. As the engineer-in-chief during the digging of the Suez Canal, he offered Ferdinand de Lesseps a partnership, with the goal of creating a railway line from Europe to India. The biggest obstacle to his plan was the number of hilly or mountainous regions which needed to be crossed. However, Charles Cotard saw many diplomatic and economic opportunities (such as closer relations between England and Russia) in this venture. The map's caption shows the new route's predicted cost and time for passengers compared to the current available routes.

b776a817-c7d7-51b1-8767-4441833fd7a5.name: *The Progress of Steam: A View in White Chapel Road, 1830*
b776a817-c7d7-51b1-8767-4441833fd7a5.second_name: Taken from Salomon's collection, *Transport, Cycles, Automobiles*
b776a817-c7d7-51b1-8767-4441833fd7a5.description2: Steam engines carried a great variety of goods in the 1830s. This English cartoon imagines the chaos the widespread use of collective and individual carbon-fuelled transport systems would bring (pollution, noise, cumbersome, etc.) to one of London's great arteries, Whitechapel Road. These vehicles provided fashionable services such as on-board coffee.

b7e5dd09-cf9b-5310-9343-8db43d0c9114.name: *The Emperor of Austria ascending the Great Pyramid*
b7e5dd09-cf9b-5310-9343-8db43d0c9114.description2: William Simpson wrote in his autobiography: "I went out one day and saw the Emperor of Austria lugged to the top of the Great Pyramid by two Arabs as if he had been only an overland passenger". Many visitors were unceremoniously hauled to the top of the monument by local inhabitants, helping unfit and often overweight tourists to clamber up the huge blocks. Emperor Franz Joseph was one of many European dignitaries in Egypt in November 1869 for the opening of the Suez Canal. Simpson was employed by the Illustrated London News as their "Special Artist". Photography would soon replace such drawings.

b8bb387e-75d0-55d8-89ae-9322c204928c.name: Simplon-Orient Express Poster
b8bb387e-75d0-55d8-89ae-9322c204928c.description2: The Orient Express, owned by the Wagon-Lits Company, connected Paris and Istanbul between 1883 and 1977. French, German, Austrian and Ottoman diplomats and civil servants were on board for its first journey. In the early years, the travellers stayed in different hotels in Istanbul but starting from 1895, passengers stayed exclusively in Pera Palace, which was bought by the Wagon-Lits Company. The Orient Express did not run during World War I, from 1914 to 1918.

b9037025-526c-5ec9-ad5b-a435eec55808.name: Travel notebook for meteorological observations
b9037025-526c-5ec9-ad5b-a435eec55808.author: Bruno Gonçalves Neves
b9037025-526c-5ec9-ad5b-a435eec55808.artist: Hermenegildo Carlos de Brito Capelo (4 February 1841, Palmela –  4 May 1917, Lisbon); photo by Rui Salta
b9037025-526c-5ec9-ad5b-a435eec55808.keywords: Capelo; Ivens; Expeditions; Africa; Angola; Mozambique
b9037025-526c-5ec9-ad5b-a435eec55808.description2: Travel notebook which belonged to Portuguese Navy’s Commander Hermenegildo Capelo, used during the expedition to the interior of the African continent in 1884/1885, from Angola’s coast to the Mozambique’s shore, along with the Portuguese Navy’s Commander Roberto Ivens. The main objective for the Portuguese expeditionary voyages in Africa was to gather all sorts of information: meteorological data, course of rivers, local inhabitants and populations, among others.

ba3b8c6f-86e6-5a4a-9b9a-6d600f5e1009.name: Archaeological excavations
ba3b8c6f-86e6-5a4a-9b9a-6d600f5e1009.description2: Portrait of three scholars in front of the tent camp during the excavations in the archaeological area of Saqqara, Giza in 1912. The paper photograph was printed from a gelatine print negative.

ba590c72-051f-5d9a-898f-073b4347852b.name: *Port, Beirut*
ba590c72-051f-5d9a-898f-073b4347852b.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
ba590c72-051f-5d9a-898f-073b4347852b.author: Stefan Weber
ba590c72-051f-5d9a-898f-073b4347852b.second_name: During the opening of the railway station at the harbour
ba590c72-051f-5d9a-898f-073b4347852b.description2: On 19/6/1887, the Ottoman authority gave the concession of the Port to an Ottoman company under the name of "Compagnie du Port, des Quais et des Entrepôts de Beyrouth". The concession was later fortified when the company gained from the Customs the sole rights to store and carry all the transit goods passing through the Customs. Constructions works namely a maritime dam to expand and develop the Port were accomplished and the opening on the occasion of the accomplishment of these works was celebrated by the end of 1894, basins were developed and spread between Ras Al Shamiah and Ras Al Mudawar. It forms the midpoint of three continents: Europe, Asia and Africa, which makes the Port a passage for ship fleets between East and West. During the mid 70's, the Port of Beirut was an important international trading station with the surrounding Arab countries and up until today it has preserved its commercial nature.

bc4ebe5a-094c-56c1-b426-f1d720ea5206.name: Abdülaziz (1830–1876)
bc4ebe5a-094c-56c1-b426-f1d720ea5206.description2: Portrait of Abdülaziz (1830–1876). In 1861 he became Sultan. He was very interested in fostering a good relationship with European powers and to this end visited Paris, London and Vienna in 1867. Because of the uprisings in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Bulgaria, he was forced to abdicate on 30 May 1876.

bd3a3ff1-4b7c-5ae4-a1d2-6d334b286559.name: Set of photos illustrating the Ducks Room, the Birds and Poultry Room, the Poultry and Egg sorting room at Fu`ad Agricultural Museum
bd3a3ff1-4b7c-5ae4-a1d2-6d334b286559.dates: 16 January 1938 (Photos taken during the inauguration of the museum)
bd3a3ff1-4b7c-5ae4-a1d2-6d334b286559.description2: The Fu`ad Agriculture Museum was considered the first of its kind in the Middle East and the Arab World during the 1930s. It was inaugurated during the time of King Faruq, the son of King Fu`ad, and houses a large number of collections related to agricultural and rural environments, as well as agricultural plants and animals.

bd95565d-ce05-5cc5-ad92-00c2e0054f8d.name: Accounting book
bd95565d-ce05-5cc5-ad92-00c2e0054f8d.keywords: architecture; railways; Haydarpaşa Train Station; Anatolian Railway
bd95565d-ce05-5cc5-ad92-00c2e0054f8d.description2: This accounting book belonged to the Anatolian Railway. On it can be seen Abdülhamid II's monogram in gilding, and the words "*Devlet-i Aliye-i Osmaniye’nin Varidat ve Mesarifat-ı Umumiyesinin Muhasebesidir*" (this book belongs to the income and expenses of the state).

be44b9c0-4045-581b-a6e2-85c0f3bcd137.name: The Austrian ship on which Emperor Franz Joseph participated at the opening ceremony of the Suez Canal in 1869
be44b9c0-4045-581b-a6e2-85c0f3bcd137.holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
be44b9c0-4045-581b-a6e2-85c0f3bcd137.description2: Emperor Franz Joseph visited the Suez Canal on board the Austrian ship, *Elisabeth*. He reached the Egyptian port of Ismilia on 14 Nov 1869 and stayed in Egypt until the 26 Nov 1869. During this trip, he also visited Cairo and Alexandria.

bf3b00b7-e2b1-52d9-ac3a-710b848a0c69.name: Medal – The construction of the Suez Canal
bf3b00b7-e2b1-52d9-ac3a-710b848a0c69.artist:
Eugène André Oudiné (1st January 1810, Paris – 12 April 1887, Paris);  
Alexis Joseph Depaulis (30 August 1792, Paris – 29 September 1867, Paris)
bf3b00b7-e2b1-52d9-ac3a-710b848a0c69.description2: Built between 1859–1869, the Suez Canal represents a direct link between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. It had a positive influence on the commerce of Europe with the southern Arabian Peninsula, as it significantly reduced the duration of transports, given that in the past a longer route, which went around Africa, was used. This bronze medal dedicated to the construction of the canal was issued in 1864. Its obverse, designed by Chaplain, features the laureate head of emperor Napoleon III. On the reverse, designed by Depaulis, is depicted Industria standing between Europe and Africa, who are holding hands. Above the three female figures is inscribed “Jonction des deux mers” (Junction of the two seas) and beyond there are emblems of Egypt (a pyramid, the Sphinx, a palm tree) and of the canal (a ship).

bff5b327-dd8c-55ac-a7f0-49d5bbc62548.name: *Works for the opening of the Corinth Canal*
bff5b327-dd8c-55ac-a7f0-49d5bbc62548.author: Maria Dimitriadou
bff5b327-dd8c-55ac-a7f0-49d5bbc62548.description2:
The Corinth Canal under constuction, circa 1885. Photographer unknown.  
The Corinth Canal separates the Peloponnesian peninsula from the Greek. The idea of the canal was revived after Greece gained independence but soon abandoned due to economical reasons. The opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 gave an new impetus and the following year, the Zaimis government passed a law authorising the construction of the canal, which was formally inaugurated on 23 April 1882. Zaimis assigned the project to the Hungarian István Türr who set up the Société Internationale du Canal Maritime de Corinthe but the company failed and the project was finished by the company of Andeas Syngros. The canal was designed by the Hungarian engineer Béla Gerster with the assistance of the French Vincent Dauzants, a chief engineer of the Suez canal.

c072d700-9ae2-5214-ad10-69e3cb6824fa.name: Film camera of the Manaki brothers
c072d700-9ae2-5214-ad10-69e3cb6824fa.holder: The Archive of the City of Bitola
c072d700-9ae2-5214-ad10-69e3cb6824fa.author: Aco Kimovski (Archive of the City of Bitola)
c072d700-9ae2-5214-ad10-69e3cb6824fa.second_name: Film camera of Charls Trade Company, serial no. 300
c072d700-9ae2-5214-ad10-69e3cb6824fa.description2: Janaki (1878–1945) and Milton (1880–1964) Manaki were born in Bitola and went on to become pioneers of Macedonian film and the first filmmakers in the Balkans. The Manaki brothers shot their first film merely 10 years after the Lumiere brothers. In 1905, they shot their grandmother Despina spinning wool with women from the neighbourhood. Their first film of ethnographic value was shot soon after. It documents celebration of the feast of St. Cyril and Methodius in front of the Church in Bitola devoted to these saints. In their films, the Manaki brothers strived to document visually events from everyday life and to frame them as real works of art. In 1921, they projected the first film in the open-air arena at the Shirok Sokak Street in Bitola.

c1d26025-2ca5-57a6-a96a-62abae4ddcf7.name: Port of Casablanca
c1d26025-2ca5-57a6-a96a-62abae4ddcf7.history: When the Port of Casablanca began trading in 1572 it was very small and known as the Port of Anfa. At this time, the port was used to export goods such as wheat and wool to the southern Mediterranean. When two centuries later, in 1785, Sultan Sidi Muhammad ibn ‘Abdallah decided to intensify trade between Morocco and countries beyond the southern Mediterranean, the port grew. A century later, in 1873, Sultan Mulay al-Hassan I launched a major project to improve the port's infrastructure and increase its capacity, and it was at this time that the commercial potential of the port was really exploited. Construction lasted several decades. In 1904, under Sultan Mulay ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, a contract was signed with the French company *Compagnie Marocaine* for the construction and development of a small port exclusively for barges that were used for loading and unloading the ships. The reorganisation in 1907 increased the harbour to 20ha. In 1921 this was increased to 140ha. In 1913 a Moroccan company and a German company, Schneider et Cie, began to co-manage the port.
c1d26025-2ca5-57a6-a96a-62abae4ddcf7.keywords: Technical innovation; communication; port; trade; commerce; economy; strategical port; strategical hub; modernisation; industrialisation; Moroccan ports; traditional port; work; urban space; changes in urban space; industrialisation and changes in urban spaces; Islamic city; Moroccan city; urban planning; plan; foreign company; French in Morocco; French in North Africa; German in Morocco; migration; southern Mediterranean; northern Mediterranean; trading route
c1d26025-2ca5-57a6-a96a-62abae4ddcf7.description2: In 1913 the port had a number of terminals under several different managements according to its wares. Terminal I, with a capacity of 7000,000 TEU, was managed by Marsa Morocco while Terminal II, with a capacity of 1,000 TEU, was managed by Somaport. There was a terminal for phosphates with a capacity of 19 million tons, operated by OCP; another for citrus with an 18.6ha capacity; and another for ore and hydrocarbons with a 14.5ha capacity. There was also a *Terminal Roulier* for vehicles, of 9.6ha capacity. After its enlargement in 1921, the port became a major international port with many warehouses, administrative offices and a large lighthouse. It had two gigantic locks, which meant that the harbour covered an area of 140 ha.

c74178c2-ab9f-5408-9cbb-cf1f4eff394d.name: Press release about Raml Tramway
c74178c2-ab9f-5408-9cbb-cf1f4eff394d.keywords: Raml Tramway; Alexandria; Mohamed Mahmoud Pasha; Transportation
c74178c2-ab9f-5408-9cbb-cf1f4eff394d.description2: A press release in the Al-Ahram newspaper regarding the Raml Tramway and related views of the Prime Minister at that time. The tramway of Alexandria was the first method of mass transportation in Egypt and in Africa, and the most common. The tramway began operating in 1860, and is thus considered the oldest tramway in Africa – and among the oldest in the world.

c88e4cac-7c3a-5acf-8cad-3a3c6bf1777f.name: Photograph: *Music School, Syria*
c88e4cac-7c3a-5acf-8cad-3a3c6bf1777f.description:
Stereoscopic photography that creates the illusion of depth of field from two apparently identical images mounted on a rigid board by using a specific viewfinder, or stereoscope.  
The images taken by the Keystone View Company show very different scenes related to lifestyles and traditions of different continents. In this case, there is a man playing a stringed instrument with a bow, possibly a type of rebec, surrounded by a group of children and two adults, who watch and listen carefully. In Syria, as in many other parts of the world, music has had and still has an important role as a means of transmitting knowledge and to celebrate individual and collective events, and is closely linked to rites, institutions, cultural and ideological activities of different humans. This image illustrates not only the practice of this activity, music, but also the transfer of knowledge from one generation to another; music serves as a vehicle of expression and relationship between members of a society.

cc27cb2b-74b2-53c7-99e4-842dcfe24334.name: The post office
cc27cb2b-74b2-53c7-99e4-842dcfe24334.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
cc27cb2b-74b2-53c7-99e4-842dcfe24334.history: Following the establishment of the French Protectorate in Tunisia, the French administration set up the post and telegraphy service in the Regency of Tunis. The post and telegraph office was created on 1 July 1888. The first Tunisian stamp was issued the following day. Finally, the Hôtel des Postes de Tunis was opened on the 11 July 1882. The first telegraph lines connecting Tunis and Marseille were soon built, and the first international communication was effectuated in November 1915 between Tunisia and Algeria.
cc27cb2b-74b2-53c7-99e4-842dcfe24334.description2: The Hôtel des PTT was designed by the architect Henri Saladin, and built on the Rue d'Italie (now called Rue Charles-de-Gaulle) in a network of straight roads lined with apartment blocks. This imposing building is designed in a Greco-Roman style. The windowless arches and huge wall clock on the main façade hint to the enormous dimensions of this municipal building's great hall. It was listed as a historic monument in 1992.

cce9ed43-6802-51d5-8553-802e6dafb35e.name: *Siever's patent pedestrian carriage for Ladies and Gentlemen*
cce9ed43-6802-51d5-8553-802e6dafb35e.description2: Many different two-wheeled cycles, such as dandy horses and velocipedes, were invented in the early 19th century. Their underlying principle was the parallel use of feet and wheels to propel the vehicle forward. They quickly become very fashionable amongst the European upper classes, who saw them as a source of entertainment, as we can see from this English print. However, it was not until the 20th century, after many alterations (pedals, etc.) that the "bicycle" became a widespread mode of transport.

cf706f6f-69db-525d-a769-9e4a92dc0759.keywords: Railway; Hijaz; station; hajj; pilgrimage; pilgrimage route; Arabian Peninsula; Saudi Arabia; sacred places; al-Madina al-Munawwara; caravan; pilgrim; Ottoman; Germany; Abdul Hamid; abd al-hamid; communication; innovation
cf706f6f-69db-525d-a769-9e4a92dc0759.description2: It is one of the tracks in al-Madina Station wrote on it the opening date of the station and the arrival of the first train to al-Madina from Istanbul.

d0602307-9a81-587d-b9b3-2b8e93c844eb.name: Al-Madina al-Munawwara Station
d0602307-9a81-587d-b9b3-2b8e93c844eb.holder: Saudi Commission for Tourism and Antiquities
d0602307-9a81-587d-b9b3-2b8e93c844eb.history:
The Hijaz railway was very important for the Islamic world where pilgrims could reach al-Hijaz safe and in short time comparing to what was before. The station was known in al-Madina as *istasyon*, a Turkish word meaning station.  
The station is located west of the Prophet 's Mohammed (PBU) Mosque and approximately 1 km a way, in the region now known Aanbariyah beside Anbariyah Mosque and Alanbariyah Gate, which was removed for the purpose of expanding the streets in the area.  
The first train arrived to al-Madina in 23rd of August 1908 and the official ceremony for the opening of the Station was held a week later.
d0602307-9a81-587d-b9b3-2b8e93c844eb.keywords: Hijaz; railway station; pilgrimage; hajj; pilgrimage route; caravan; sacred places; communication; innovation; architecture; Arabian Peninsula; Ottoman; Germany; Abdul Hamid; abd al-hamid

d0602307-9a81-587d-b9b3-2b8e93c844eb.description2: The station is rectangular in shape with a length of about 700 meters and a width of about 150 meters, and is surrounded by a fence built of black basalt stone, and comprises a set of 11 buildings including the main one. All the station buildings and remaining trains and carriages were restored by the Saudi commission for Tourism and Antiquities and converted into an Islamic museum for the city of al-Madina.

d1281641-f7a2-5961-be72-73fcc5949104.name: Telegraph transmitter
d1281641-f7a2-5961-be72-73fcc5949104.keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication
d1281641-f7a2-5961-be72-73fcc5949104.description2: The primary reasons for the Ottoman Empire adopting the telegram earlier and more easily than railroads were the telegram's convenience and lack of cost. American scientist Lawrence Smith – using tools sent by Samuel Morse – made a successful trial in front of the Sultan Abdulmecid, who was interested in technological innovations and science, and began modernization of the empire. Due to the outbreak of the Crimean War, the first underwater telegraph line was established between Crimea and Istanbul. This telegraph transmitter (1912, Siemens & Halske) was used in Istanbul in World War I.

d571791c-a497-50be-b648-cbb508ceae8f.name: Manifestation celebrating King Fu`ad I
d571791c-a497-50be-b648-cbb508ceae8f.keywords: King Fu`ad; Fayum Directorate; new roads; The Royal Road
d571791c-a497-50be-b648-cbb508ceae8f.description2: Fayum Directorate Arabs at the reception of King Fu`ad I. Fu`ad I ruled Egypt from 9 October 1917 to 28 April 1936. During his reign, the 1919 revolution began, and the British had to end Egypt's status as a protectorate and declare it an independent country with sovereignty. Independence was declared on 15 March 1922. Also during his reign, the first public ministry was established in January 1924, headed by Sa`d Zaghlul. King Fu`ad had a number of important accomplishments, and for this reason this photo was chosen – to manifest King Fu`ad's concern with roads, especially the royal road towards the Fayum Directorate.

d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.name: Barbadinhos Steam pumping station
d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.holder: EPAL- Portuguese Society for Water Supply
d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.author: Bárbara Bruno
d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.history: Classified as CIP – Setting of Public Interest through Decree. º 1176/2010, DR, 2nd Series, no. 248 of 14/12/2010, the Station of Barbadinhos was designed to raise water from the Alviela river to the reservoir of Veronica and to the Cistern of Monte. Opened on 3 October 1880, the station considerably increased the volume of water supplied to the city of Lisbon. Its main equipment, consisting of four steam engines built in the workshops of E. W. Windsor of Rouen, ran until 1928.
d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.keywords: Lisbon water supply; Steam Machinery; Water Museum; Barbadinhos; industrial archaeology building
d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.architects: Windsor House & Fils and Workshops of CAL – Companhia das Águas de Lisboa (Water Company of Lisbon)
d616de70-37f8-5d6d-9c22-8c4a59417e94.description2: This Lisbon Water Museum is the urban memory symbol of innovation and improvements in public health issues. The Barbadinhos Steam Pumping Station opened on 3 October 1880. It was built to raise the water coming from the Alviela Canal to the Veronica and Cisterna do Monte reservoirs. It was used to increase the volume of the water supplied to the city of Lisbon. The main equipment consists of four steam machines that worked uninterruptedly until 1928. They were built in the workshops of “Constructeurs - Mecaniciens” E. W. Windsor & Fils, of Rouen, France, an English owned company. The machines, whose steam was produced by five boilers, are all of the same kind: vertical pistons with two cylinders each and steam liner – Woolf system – of variable expansion and condensation.

d6ede956-3098-5ac6-8afc-b9788d8dd31f.holder: Musée des Postes, Télégraphes et Télécommunications
d6ede956-3098-5ac6-8afc-b9788d8dd31f.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
d6ede956-3098-5ac6-8afc-b9788d8dd31f.keywords: Painted wood; floral decoration; Turkish influences; European influences
d6ede956-3098-5ac6-8afc-b9788d8dd31f.description2: The objects assembled in this room all date to the late 19th century and belong to a set of urban Tunisian furnishings. These articles were all part of Tunis' first municipal postmaster's office. They consist of four chairs and a bench in painted wood, centred around a two-layered desk, painted in a floral motif on a pale blue background. Behind, a shelving unit, painted in the same style. This furnishing set shows evidence of traditional Tunisian, Turkish and various European influences.

d815fe5d-36cb-5efe-b0e0-241a5e5e2941.name: Stamp sketch
d815fe5d-36cb-5efe-b0e0-241a5e5e2941.keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication
d815fe5d-36cb-5efe-b0e0-241a5e5e2941.description2: The Ottoman Empire held a contest to determine the stamp that would be printed in London between 1919 and 1921. Stamp sketches drawn by famous calligraphers are exhibited in the museum. This stamp sketch belonged to the Eminönü Post Office.

d86bffa6-0320-50d5-b0a4-c47134d7d642.name: Water pumping equipment in Kağıthane, Istanbul
d86bffa6-0320-50d5-b0a4-c47134d7d642.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
d86bffa6-0320-50d5-b0a4-c47134d7d642.keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph; History of Water in Ottoman Empire; Water Pump Station
d86bffa6-0320-50d5-b0a4-c47134d7d642.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. Cendere Hamidian Water Pump Station was built by Abdülhamid II in 1902 at an altitude of 34 metres above sea level. With its function, architectural design and mechanical equipment, the station is a unique monument to the history of the architecture industry in the Ottoman Empire. It pumped to Balmumcu and Beşiktaş – in the direction of Tophane, moving water coming from 20 different pipes in Kağıthane using steam pump machines.

d8d34fe2-1034-53c0-ae9e-ca9794a01c63.name: Railway Bridge from Anatolia
d8d34fe2-1034-53c0-ae9e-ca9794a01c63.holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)

d8d34fe2-1034-53c0-ae9e-ca9794a01c63.description2: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.

dfc4cc0b-d5f3-5aa9-a482-5dd72c63bdf8.name: Map of the Red Sea
dfc4cc0b-d5f3-5aa9-a482-5dd72c63bdf8.author: Maria Francesca Carvelli (MWNF)
dfc4cc0b-d5f3-5aa9-a482-5dd72c63bdf8.archival: *The Red Sea Pilot ... With directions for the navigation of the Suez Canal. Second edition. \[Compiled by J. C. Richards\]*, *Sailing Directions. Red Sea*, London: Hydrographic Office, 1883, third edition
dfc4cc0b-d5f3-5aa9-a482-5dd72c63bdf8.keywords: Trade; route; port; Great Britain; India; coffee; Red Sea; Yemen; Mocha; British settlement on the route to India; communication; telegraph; telegraph between ports; Suez Canal; pilgrimage; Makka; Arab Peninsula; Holy places
dfc4cc0b-d5f3-5aa9-a482-5dd72c63bdf8.description2:
*The Red Sea Pilot* included sailing indications and directions for navigation from the Suez Canal to the strait of Bab el-Mandeb, including Aqaba, Jeddah and the coast of Hijaz as far as Aden.  
  
Trading activity (especially in grain) between the two coasts of the Red Sea and the maritime traffic after the opening of the Suez Canal were fundamental economic activities, hence the importance of reliable knowledge of navigation routes, sailing directions, climate, winds and currents. In addition to the local ships used to carry pilgrims to Mecca and for trading activity, European ships crossed the Red Sea. The book also provides information about the main ports and their facilities. For example, it states that the telegraph had been installed from Suez to Swakin and from Swakin to Jeddah, and that there was telegraph communication between Aden, Suez, Bombay and the Cape of Good Hope.

e1be7517-b6b1-576b-8acd-653f24c29ba9.name: *Hijaz Railway Station, Damascus*
e1be7517-b6b1-576b-8acd-653f24c29ba9.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
e1be7517-b6b1-576b-8acd-653f24c29ba9.author: Stefan Weber
e1be7517-b6b1-576b-8acd-653f24c29ba9.second_name: Main Station of the Hijaz railway leading from Damascus to Medina
e1be7517-b6b1-576b-8acd-653f24c29ba9.description2: The Hijaz station was originally built in 1903 to provide faster transportation for Pilgrims to Medina. So the today closed-down railway station used to be an essential transport and communication link. Furthermore it was built to integrate aloof provinces better into the Ottoman state and hence establish a closer political and economic connection. The new building completed in 1917 also embodies a desire for innovation in terms of design: its architecture is a mix between traditional local Ottoman elements and monumentalizing features of historicism.

e2b48175-dfa4-5317-9f12-0d280735f099.name: Drawing of the railway bridge between the mainland and Venice
e2b48175-dfa4-5317-9f12-0d280735f099.description2: This panoramic view shows the railway link between Venice and the mainland. In 1837 a company was founded to organize the building of the railway in the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia. Construction started in 1840 and the railway reached the Venetian station of Santa Lucia in 1846.

e2ed7029-baf0-5a6c-b94c-553bba5ed68d.name: Medal commemorating the opening of the Suez Canal
e2ed7029-baf0-5a6c-b94c-553bba5ed68d.description2: This silver medal designed by O. Roty was struck in 1869, to mark the opening of the Suez Canal, which was built to connect the Mediterranean directly to the Red Sea. On the obverse of the medal is depicted a seated female figure holding the light of Progress in front of the standing figure of Industry. Beyond there is a sketched route of the Suez Canal. In the centre and on the margin of the reverse there are two inscriptions: “Le 17 novembre 1869 le canale maritime a été ouvert à la grande navigation” (On the 17th November 1869 the maritime canal was opened for heavy navigation) and “Compagnie Universelle du Canal Maritime de Suez” (Universal Company of the Suez Maritime Canal). On the coin’s rim is inscribed “L’epargne française prepare la paix du monde” (The French thrift prepares the world peace).

e3029e51-8121-5e09-b08a-bd958da4cd09.name: 'The first railway engine in Tripoli'
e3029e51-8121-5e09-b08a-bd958da4cd09.author: Giulia Barrera
e3029e51-8121-5e09-b08a-bd958da4cd09.description2:
The railway in a colonial context was much more than a means of transport: it was a powerful symbol of modernity, of technological superiority of the colonisers over the colonised, and of mastery over the territory. The construction of railways in colonial situations was often celebrated by the colonialists’ popular press or in postcards, as in this case.  
In Libya, the Italians started building railroads from the first months of colonial rule. The first lines, inaugurated in 1912, connected Tripoli with Ain Zara (11 kms) and to Zanzur (39 kms). By the end of 1915, the railway lines in Libya amounted to 180 kilometres.

e3b28f28-4ce6-5e60-9902-8e13ef295f77.name: Photograph of Tétouan Railway Station
e3b28f28-4ce6-5e60-9902-8e13ef295f77.description: The image does not give one a sense of the real scale of Tétouan Railway Station, one of the first to be built in Morocco in 1918, covering an area of about 1,200m2 and comprises three buildings: one castle-shaped and two large hangars. The station is a model of colonial architecture, bearing the signature of Julio Rodriguez Roda, an engineer working for the Spanish Society of Colonisation, which was responsible for many structures in northern Morocco. Receiving its first travellers at the end of World War I, the line stretched from Tétouan to Ceuta, calling at Martil, Ben Karrich and Zinat.

e3d1028e-c33d-53a4-a895-0276547994a0.name: *Construction of the Bordeaux bridge in 1821*
e3d1028e-c33d-53a4-a895-0276547994a0.second_name: Taken from the collection *Topographie de la France*, "Département de la Gironde"
e3d1028e-c33d-53a4-a895-0276547994a0.description2: The construction of bridges had always been a complicated matter, and particularly so in Bordeaux, where the river was especially temperamental. Until the 19th century people crossed it by ferry. However, in 1810 Napoléon I ordered a bridge to be built in Bordeaux, which was completed in 1822. The expertise this required (particularly the building of tunnels to reduce the size of the structure) attracted the attention of many contemporary engineers and architects.

e89aa553-0859-53ef-ad91-bdaddb8ac231.name: *Hüdavendigar* Paper in Armenian
e89aa553-0859-53ef-ad91-bdaddb8ac231.description2: After the *Tanzimat* (reforms), newspapers in Arabic, Persian, Bulgarian, Serbian, Albanian, Kurdish, English, French, Italian and German began appearing in the Ottoman Empire. Some of them were bilingual as Turkish-Greek, Turkish-Armenian and Turkish-Arabic. *Hüdavendigar* was a provincial newspaper of Bursa and it was first published on 19 February 1869. The same year, starting with the 80th issue, the back page was printed in Armenian. The paper was published twice (Wednesday and Saturday) and then four times a week. It was 50 x 25 cm. Subscription for a year was 100 kuruş, for six months was 50 kuruş and one issue was 20 para (1/2 kuruş). It continued to be published until 1953 under different names.

e92c5fac-cccf-5730-b2e6-c7774c2761e7.name: The paved road between Beirut and Damascus
e92c5fac-cccf-5730-b2e6-c7774c2761e7.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Rita El Hachem
e92c5fac-cccf-5730-b2e6-c7774c2761e7.description2: This paved road was constructed between over a period of six years, between 1857 and 1863. It measured six metres in width and facilitated the circulation of horse-drawn carriages owned by the "diligence" transportation company.

ea1f55bf-b075-5e73-a04a-db3e93d8bff2.name: Revolver
ea1f55bf-b075-5e73-a04a-db3e93d8bff2.description:
According to the engraving on the barrel, this revolver was manufactured by J. Nikittis Erben in Constantinople. Erben was a revolver-maker and retailer who sold Colt firearms. Another engraving also reads ""POUCARTOUCHE NAGANT"". The serial number was engraved on the left side of the revolver right under the cylinder. Only the last two digits (76) can be seen. The revolver is fitted with wooden grips and fixed to the frame by a screw. This  
revolver is similar to the Swiss revolver of 1882, but not identical. It might be a variation of that revolver.

ea3a91f8-4029-5f91-8e55-44b4089bf748.name: *Bayt al-Barudi steamship murals, Damascus*
ea3a91f8-4029-5f91-8e55-44b4089bf748.holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
ea3a91f8-4029-5f91-8e55-44b4089bf748.author: Stefan Weber
ea3a91f8-4029-5f91-8e55-44b4089bf748.second_name: Mural in the main reception hall of the Barudi House at the quarter of Qanawat
ea3a91f8-4029-5f91-8e55-44b4089bf748.description2: The steamships are of one of the most important technical innovations in the nineteenth-century, because they introduced new modern possibilities of transport and trade and hence contributed to the economic transformation of the Ottoman Empire. Because of this new transportation, cities on the Euphrates or Tigris experienced drastic changes and flourished even more. This impact lead to numerous depictions of steamships in artwork, such as this mural from Bayt al-Qabbani (Damascus, built at the turn of the 19th/20th century) shows. As symbols of the new time they represent global exchange of goods, ideas and people.

ea68ca74-8e7f-519d-98cf-82fb84aa3d58.name: Medal to commemorate the inauguration of Ma'an station
ea68ca74-8e7f-519d-98cf-82fb84aa3d58.keywords: Numismatics; Hijaz; Hijaz Railway; Ottoman empire; 'Abd al-Hamid; railway; pilgrimage; Hijaz; sharif; Makka al-Mukarrama; Mecca; al-Madina al-Munawwara; Medina; Ottoman imperial symbols; monogram; Ottoman monograms

On the obverse is the *tuğra* of Sultan ‘Abd al-Hamid II with the inscription “al-Ghazi” and the image of a locomotive. On the reverse is the date (AH) 1322.

ebc1fbff-c25e-5ca5-86ba-1be3dbc34cbf.name: The Gallery of Machines – Section of French Telegraphic Machines, Marinoni's Continuous Paper Model [Paris Exhibition, 1878]
ebc1fbff-c25e-5ca5-86ba-1be3dbc34cbf.author: Marina Minozzi
ebc1fbff-c25e-5ca5-86ba-1be3dbc34cbf.archival: *L'Esposizione di Parigi del 1878 illustrata*, Sonzogno Editore, 1878, p. 245
