ebc1fbff-c25e-5ca5-86ba-1be3dbc34cbf.third_name: *La galleria delle macchine: – sezione francese Macchine telegrafiche, modello Marinoni a carta continua*
ebc1fbff-c25e-5ca5-86ba-1be3dbc34cbf.description2: Two of the most important inventions of the 19th century, the rotary and four-colour printing (quadrachrome), are attributed to Augusto Ippolito Marinoni. The new machines changed the printing of journals, achieving up to 18,000 to 20,000 copies per hour. Marinoni had extraordinary success in Paris, where his factory produced 4000 samples of machines which also sold in London, Berlin and Vienna. In Italy at the time, only the journal *Il Secolo* had a "Marinoni".

ef89ce14-252d-5bb0-8014-da9c14164139.name: *Egypt. Construction of the Suez canal: the construction workers*
ef89ce14-252d-5bb0-8014-da9c14164139.keywords: Suez canal; Egypt; Ferdinand de Lesseps
ef89ce14-252d-5bb0-8014-da9c14164139.second_name: Taken from *Canal Maritime de Suez: Photographies D'apres Nature par Justin Kozlowski*
ef89ce14-252d-5bb0-8014-da9c14164139.description2: Photographers such as Justin Kozlowski photographed the excavation works throughout the construction of the Suez Canal. In contrast to the usual photos of Egypt which were taken for tourists, photographs such as this were taken for documentary purposes: it allowed the Suez Canal Company to see the progress and cost of the works.

efe60dc6-7155-5eb3-a180-d0bfbd548106.name: Revenue stamp
efe60dc6-7155-5eb3-a180-d0bfbd548106.description2: A revenue stamp issued in 1888 during the reign of Khedive Muhammad Tawfiq with the value of one dime. Written at the top is “Egypt Post” in Arabic with its French translation below it. To the left is the value of the dime in French, and in the centre is an image of one of the Giza pyramids and the Sphinx. The first postal stamp was issued in England in 1840. It bore the portrait of Queen Victoria, as suggested by Sir Roland Hill. This stamp was issued twice, in red and in blue. The United States of America was the second country in the world to use stamps, and the first Egyptian stamp was issued in 1866 by order of Khedive Ismail.

f0e5d0e1-0d9f-5dac-9166-a688b53727f8.name: Zaghwan aqueduct
f0e5d0e1-0d9f-5dac-9166-a688b53727f8.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
f0e5d0e1-0d9f-5dac-9166-a688b53727f8.history: Water problems were one of the Tunisian governments' constant preoccupations. It was the custom for wealthy people to build public fountains called *sabils*. Rulers, however, were preoccupied with the organisation of large scale water conveyance. In 1859, just before the establishment of the French protectorate and on the advice of the French consul Léon Roches, Mohamed Bey tasked the engineer Pierre Colin with the restoration of the old Roman aqueduct running from Zaghwan to Carthage, and its Hafsid era diversion towards Tunis, which had been out of use and abandoned for a long time. The works were completed in 1862, during Mohamed Sadok Bey's reign.
f0e5d0e1-0d9f-5dac-9166-a688b53727f8.description2: The hydraulic works are described in the general administration's 1883–1889 Public Works report as follows: "89 km of brick canal between Zaghwan and Goulette were refurbished, 41 km of metal piping has replaced the huge aqueducts at Djouggar, Oued Miliane, Djedeida and the Aryanah plains". Water supplies for Tunis and the beylical residences were thus assured. The piping was put into operation for the first time on 19 May 1862. You can still see the impressive row of columns and arches today.

f12fed73-12b9-5991-a430-4273cea32560.name: Revolver
f12fed73-12b9-5991-a430-4273cea32560.description: A Liege/ Belgium manufactured revolver. Some of these revolvers were produced in Liege by the Leon Nagant factory for the Russian army between 1895 and 1898 (The Belgian Contract Revolvers), but some other revolvers of this type were produced in Russia itself (Tula) after that. The revolver is fitted with chequered grip plates that are fixed to the frame with a screw installed in a round steel insert. On the left side of the revolver the word Liege was engraved preceded by two illegible words. Only the last letter S can be clearly seen. Right under the word Liege two words were completely erased. On the barrel from the right side of the revolver a crowned oval with the letter R in the middle was engraved. Under the oval a star with what might be a letter g is engraved. The same letter is repeated on the frame at the base of the barrel.

f31fd223-2144-5b45-8b4a-8cf3c4d36bc5.name: *London-Paris-Constantinople* \[…\] *Orient Express. Paris-Munich-Vienna-Budapest-Belgrade & Constantinople: fast and direct service, without your car and without your passport* \[…\] *Winter 1888–89 ...*
f31fd223-2144-5b45-8b4a-8cf3c4d36bc5.description2: Founded in 1872, the Compagnie Internationale des Wagons-lits was originally a Belgian company. Its founder (Georges Nagelmackers) had the idea of creating a luxury train line, without the need for changes at each border, in order to allow wealthier tourists a more comfortable journey. The opening of the famous Orient Express between Paris and Constantinople in 1883 was an extremely successful example of this.

f5b47725-414d-52d8-902a-bee467f7d304.name: *Works for the opening of the Corinth Canal*
f5b47725-414d-52d8-902a-bee467f7d304.author: Maria Dimitriadou
f5b47725-414d-52d8-902a-bee467f7d304.description2:
The Corinth Canal being dug, circa 1885. Photographer unknown.  
The Corinth Canal separates the Peloponnesian peninsula from the Greek. The idea of the canal was revived after Greece gained independence but soon abandoned due to economical reasons. The opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 gave an new impetus and the following year, the Zaimis government passed a law authorising the construction of the canal, which was formally inaugurated on 23 April 1882. Zaimis assigned the project to the Hungarian István Türr who set up the Société Internationale du Canal Maritime de Corinthe but the company failed and the project was finished by the company of Andeas Syngros. The canal was designed by the Hungarian engineer Béla Gerster with the assistance of the French Vincent Dauzants, a chief engineer of the Suez canal.

fb87a426-40c2-5d5c-a3d0-e7ba69ca00e7.name: *The railway*
fb87a426-40c2-5d5c-a3d0-e7ba69ca00e7.second_name: Part of the rail transport system
fb87a426-40c2-5d5c-a3d0-e7ba69ca00e7.description2: Epinal prints take their name from the eponymous town in the Vosges region of France. These stencil-coloured lithographies with simple designs became very popular during the 19th century, thanks to their modest price and popular themes. This particular print is aimed at explaining the new railway system to rural communities, by illustrating the different jobs related to this mode of transport (station master, porter), and the types of people interested in faster transportation (soldiers, tourists, merchants). The different classes (from first to third) and their varying levels of comfort are also shown. This helped dispel and ridicule the fear transport had evoked.

fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.name: Portrait of the Marquess of Cerralbo in a Turkish Garment
fc3b1ec9-a4c8-5bb0-8563-67addfda87dd.description: The Marquis of Cerralbo and his family visited Istanbul in 1889, and nowadays the Cerralbo Museum holds an interesting variety of pieces bought and collected as souvenirs from the family trip. When visiting a foreign country or city, being portraited by a famous photographer of studio was indispensable. In this case the photographers are the world-renowned Armenian Abdullah Frères, Photographes de S. M. I. le Sultan. This vignetted bust shot albumen portrait of Inocencia Serrano y Cerver, marquise of Cerralbo, shows the playful and aesthetic use of typical Turkish costume in the Abdullah Frères studio, perfect to satisfy the European desire of exoticism.

ffecc84b-856d-5f87-97de-682a1d90e53d.name: *View of Istanbul: the Valide Sultan Mosque and the port*
ffecc84b-856d-5f87-97de-682a1d90e53d.second_name: Taken from the collection *Photographies Positives* by Pascal Sébah
ffecc84b-856d-5f87-97de-682a1d90e53d.description2: Pascal Sébah (1823–1886) was a French photographer working in the Ottoman capital Constantinople, where he developed a successful trade selling photographs to European tourists and lovers of Orientalism. The great changes Constantinople underwent towards the end of the 19th century are evident in this image. The Valide Sutlan Mosque dominates the Eminönü port, which had become very prosperous during the Ottoman era thanks to active trading with the West. The construction of the Galata bridge, the Orient Express railway line, and the arrival of steam-boats also contributed to its development.
